text:

In about 23 hours the charge was 20% without actively using the watch at all or turning on the screen. It is absolutely horrible. Dormant watch consumed 80% of power.

I am wearing Huawei 6 band for a week and it is still running on the same charge, it's around 15% now. It has the same sport and health functions like Samsung watch and I paid $40 for it. It is also not cumbersome like Samsung watch.

Samsung needs to fix their battery life. Thinking about return.

ECG tracker stopped working. When I try to run it on the watch , it says "New version is available. Install the update from Galaxy App Store to continue using the app. If I click on the Update button on the watch, I get "Page not found" on the phone browser.

I've been through several support chats, calls, sms, they tried to remote to my phone! and still the issue with the watch was not solved. Every support team was trying to send me somewhere else. I spent several hours talking to Samsung support.

The issue with this watch is that it is using Samsung's own home brewed half-baked operating system. It is clunky. It is misleading. If you opened some app like browser on the watch, there is no way to close it. It is running draining power. I was able to resolve the ECG app issue on yhe watch by reinstalling Galaxy Wear app on my phone. It was just a wild guess. The watch tips and Samsung support troubleshooting was absolutely useless. This watch is a bad news.

title: May change my life
text:
Because Amazon sometimes confuses products in their reviews, this is for the Garmin Venu SQ watch.

After several years of accidents, surgeries, and the lethargy that comes with a shutdown, I recognized an urgent need to change behavior. This watch was the trigger to that change and I'm very impressed.

Firstly, I don't like watches. It's been 30 years since I wore a wristwatch and I'm not quick to change. However, this watch is light and thin and nearly unnoticeable. I did replace the band with a nice wrap-around velcro model that is much more comfortable than a clasp-type band. That improved my opinion, too.

This watch tells me about my heart rate, my respiration rate, my stress levels, some very interesting information about my sleep, and it even tells time.

I feel informed about my heart health and my daily routine in a way I could not imagine before.

I also feel certain that many of the spandex and ripped-t-shirt crowd at my gym would find it inadequate for their iron-pumping and celery-smoothie lifestyles. For them, a $600 watch might be an appropriate purchase. For me, a nice entry-level watch that tracks so many things I didn't know a watch could track is more than sufficient.

I have much to learn from my watch.

The software installed on my iPhone easily and helped me set up the watch quickly.

The one "problem" with the watch was that the native language was not set up as my language, and I'm no polyphone. I found some good instructions on the interwebs that told me to press "this," then scroll down this many places and select the option found there. Then go two steps to here. It was like a school locker combination: 5 steps down, two steps right, two steps down... I didn't understand any of the words on the screen until I got to the label that said "English." Once pressed, my watch and I communicated much better.

title: Sorry Samsung... It just isn't working out between us.
text:
It's not me. It's you. The background is I've been a long time Samsung user, having started with the S7 active and then Galaxy Gear Watch 2 way back 2016. The Samsung Health app is awesome for tracking all-around fitness, from calories to cycling routes (I have become an avid distance cyclist). Unfortunately, despite having a top-rate fitness app, their products, and now their customer service, are simply lagging. It is apparent from the changes in Samsung Health that they are moving more towards a walled-garden approach like Apple. They've removed support for connected apps (like Google Fit) with the exception of Strava, and the list of non-Samsung devices they support in the fitness band Arena now contains a paltry list of sub-par discontinued products from other vendors. They want you to use Samsung devices, which is fine, BUT...

They haven't addressed a HUGE shortcoming in their wearables, which is battery life. Why is it that I can get a wearable from Garmin, Coros, or Polar that can last 20-30 hours with GPS active and 1-4 weeks without it, but Samsung still, after almost a decade making wearables, can't produce one that can last a full day of normal use? I had this problem with my original Galaxy Gear Watch 2 - it would be dead by the time I went to bed every night, and after a couple years simply wouldn't charge at all - and now several generations later the complaints about battery life are already pouring in?

I do love the Samsung Health app, and was very reluctant to change, but even the worst relationships have their bright spots. Riding over a hundred miles a week on top of having work and children takes dedication and sacrifice. I was willing to try to work within the confines of the poor battery life and use phone GPS tracking on long rides to continue using it. I wasn't happy about being forced into that decision, but was willing to accept it. So... after researching sports watches for weeks and agonizing over an expensive gadget, I pulled the trigger and pre-ordered.

I received a delivery date and when it arrived, anxiously awaited the package since I had a half-century ride planned that weekend. Except it didn't arrive. Finally that evening I got a notification that the shipment was being delayed and it would be another 5 days. Now, if the product hasn't arrived from the manufacturer, you'd think someone would have figured out how to let customers know at some point before the evening it was supposed to be at my door. So... I awaited for the new date. And when that date arrived, it said, "Arriving today by 10pm." Except once again it didn't, and I was given yet another delivery date two weeks away. The next day I finally cancelled the order, only to see that it had finally shipped and should arrive the following day. Nice. I had a twinge of remorse, but it was very slight. I broke up with Samsung, found other fitness tracking apps, synced my rides with Strava, and I'm done being held hostage by overpriced gadgets really meant to be consumer toys.

Thanks Samsung and Amazon for the disappointing experience with this one. Now I have accessories that I have to drive out of my way to return to get the rest of my money back. I understand things get delayed. What I don't understand is when that delay can't be communicated in a timely fashion. You sold a product on pre-order and gave a delivery date when apparently it was already being reported that supply was an issue, then failed to let customers know what was going on until the last minute. Not cool, and considering the reports of bugs and poor battery life (surprise) are already flooding in, time to pick something else.

title: Poor battery, inaccurate heartbeat, incoming line calls dont work, shealth bad, etc
text:
This watch is absolutely useless. I have an Apple 6 watch (and had a 5 before). Where do I even start?

1) The battery will not last anywhere close to a day
2) Heartbeat sensor is inaccurate. Sometimes it says my heart rate is a very unrealistic number which I know it isn't. It is basically useless
3) When I get an incoming call on my Line application, there is no way to answer the call using my galaxy fold 3, however I cannot answer it on my watch either, it beeps/rings on my watch but no matter where I click on the screen or buttons, there is no way to actually answer the call. So it removed my ability to answer calls at all from the Line application
4) When I get a line notification, there is a lot of swiping involved to actually read the notification
5) The apple watch allows you to have a custom info widget on the main screen, which includes support for a compass direction. The direction is automatically displayed just by raising your watch it displays N, Ne, S, whatever direction you are facing. Galaxy watch has no such ability. The compass on the Galaxy watch app requires you to do a crappy figure 8 motion to calibrate it, and it works just as horribly as it does on android phones (that is a big reason why I need a watch, because android often shows inaccurate facing direction in google maps, for 10+ years it has not been fixed- IOS doesn't have this issue at all).
6) A bunch of super annoying stuff is enabled as a default. Your watch will be vibrating all the time just to tell you that you are walking somewhere. The thing is I want the sleep function but I don't want all of the auto tracking and other annoying notifications (which no doubt make the battery life so bad). Shealth doesn't seem to have the ability to tweak enough to make this possible. If I walk 10 minutes to the train station, I get a notification that I'm walking. So I start ignoring my notifications. I want to be notified ONLY for line messages, nothing else. I turned off notifications for shealth and it still buzzes whenever I walk somewhere. I hate it, I just want to throw this watch in the toilet. I googled it and there are outdated instructions which no longer work because Samsung changes stuff around constantly. I want ONLY manual workouts, I don't want it to automatically decide I am working out just because I'm not sleeping on the couch all day. I also want to manually start my sleep tracking. There must be a way, but I can't find it. Oh, and you have to register with samsung health and give them acccess to a bunch of stuff just to be able to use the sleep tracker at all. I don't want a samsung health account but I am forced to have one.
7) The google map navigation is useless. You need to be able to see your entire route or be able to zoom out to see your entire route when driving/walking/bicyling because google will sometimes auto switch the route to something that doesn't make sense and you need to know about it. If you just blindly follow the updated route on your watch, you will run into problems, for example end up on tiny small streets on your bicycle and waste a lot of time trying to get back to the main road, etc. I could just uninstall the maps app on the watch to avoid it popping up while im navigating and want the compass shown instead.
8) There is no nosie meter. The apple watch has a noise meter which can also be displayed on the watch face next to the compasss. All the information I want is there available on the main watch face. Samsung watch faces are much more limited in the information they allow you to display.
9) custom fix watch band is fitted and made available at the Apple store so you don't need a to adjust a band, it slips on your wrist and fits perfectly. My local Samsung store doesn't have this service.
10) no voice assistant. Apple watch you hold the watch up to your mouth and talk and you have full access to siri.
11) Apple watch is smaller and fits perfectly on my wrist. I can't even tell I have it on.

I have decided to scrap my galaxy watch 4 because it is basically useless. The only function it performs correctly is displaying time and notifications (except for all of the junk notifications like auto tracking walking- Im sure there is a way to disable this but I gave up trying to find it). I am going to try having my galaxy fold 3 in wifi tethering mode constantly and having my watch connected to its hotspot, and see if I can receive Line notifications that way (I have an iphone I leave at home connected to the internet). I'm really suprised it is so bad because of all the positive reviews. I even tested it at the samsung store- you don't know all of this stuff until you make the mistake of buying it. I haven't found an android watch that comes anywhere close to the functionality of the apple watch.

title: Resets itself/looses data.  HORRIBLE documentation
text:
For some reason, it seems that the $100 price point is the dividing line for Amazfit products being decent/working well, and not. To explain..... I have purchased 3 Amazfit watches, starting with this one. There are issues and disappointments with all of them, however, this particular watch worked OK for about 4 days/nights, then it would randomly reset itself, and in the process delete all data it had accumulated. That was what made me return it.
A couple of very annoying things with this particular watch....
1. SP02 has no automatic feature/setting. Meaning that the only way it will take a reading is if you do it manually.
2. The zepp app that is required with these watches is annoying because each watch displays a bit differently on the app, due to various watches having given functions or not. But the real annoyance is syncing data, which seems to have a mind of its own.... if I try to make it sync sometimes it will, and other times not.
3. DO NOT believe the claims on battery life! With the features I wanted turned on, the best I could get was 2 days/nights on a charge!
4. Finally, ALL of the Amazfit products I've purchased have absolutely horrible documentation! The included manual is very ambiguous, and you can't figure out how anything works using it. I had to search the web and comb through far too many YouTube videos to find the information needed. The amount of time and effort wasted searching for "how to" information is enough cause a 1 star rating!

Many online reviews rate this watch as "Best Cheap Smart Watch"...... but I'd highly recommend either going with another brand at this price point, or higher price points in this brand. Go with their GTR or S or higher. I think their GTR/S 2e is the best bang for the buck, although it has the same faults and horrible documentation as the rest.

title: Love this Garmin!
text:
First off, I'm a personal trainer and triathlete, and I've been a Garmin fan for years - their devices last a long time, and are the best at fitness tracking. Have been using a 920XT for maybe 10 years(?) now and it's still working great. What I loved about it most was the triathlon mode, and loved least was the Dick Tracy watch size of the thing. I was hesistant to switch to wrist-based HRM at first, but I think the tech on these has improved dramatically, as shown by my new Garmin Venu. Here are my pro's & con's:
Pro's:
- Lightweight, extremely comfortable, no metal in the buckle (I'm allergic to nickel, used in most watch buckles)
- Beautiful screen, easy to navigate and set up (like my 920XT was)
- Battery life is as promised. I'm getting about 7 or 8 days before needing to recharge.
- Accurate HR, sleep, and run tracking - again, a Garmin strength
- The lavendar is an absolutely gorgeous color
- Accompanying phone app is Garmin's standard app, with lots of good information and easy to build workouts (but I'd recommend doing this on the web app instead.)
- Garmin syncs to Final Surge, the online training log app I use
- Has all the exercise modalities I use, and lots more: swimming outdoors, swimming in pool, biking indoors, bike outside, run indoors, run track, run outside/road, yoga, strength training, hiking.
- Allows me to see phone notifications (that I want to see, can shut off those I don't) and quickly dismiss incoming calls (like those annoying daily car warranty robocalls)
Cons:
- When running outdoors and doing intervals, it doesn't "beep" very loudly at all - it's mostly a vibration. Wish this were louder, as my 920XT was.
- Step tracking isn't very accurate - but I have yet to find ANY device that does this well. It's all based on arm movements. I did 15 steps today before getting out of bed! But seriously, don't let this discourage you...it's as good a step tracker as anything else out there.
- The strength training mode is a little wonky - haven't figured out how it supposedly counts reps. But I just tend to ignore that anyway, as my strength training for myself and my clients is very movement-oriented, not just stationary lifts.
- This model doesn't download music (there's a more expensive version if you want that). But personally this was irrelevant to me as I play my music through a bluetooth speaker when I'm inside, and I don't listen to music at all when I'm training outside.
- The price is a little high as this category of devices goes, but way cheaper than an Apple watch and without all the excess fluff those have. But much, much better than a $35-$45 cheap fitness watch. You get what you pay for.
Overall I highly recommend this watch for any fitness enthusiast.

text:
It's been disappointing from day one of getting this watch. As a galaxy phone user, I decided to upgrade from a 7 year old watch to this, thinking it can only be better. I was so wrong... Bugs that I've noticed so far:

1. Always on display is dim, so when running outside in the sun you can't see anything. There's no way to make it brighter, you have to touch the watch/raise wrist to turn it back on, rendering AOD worthless

3. There is no heart rate zone training in the app. Old watch has it
4. Can't adjust your heart rate zones. My maximum heart rate is much higher than the watch has by default which makes all of my zones wrong. My old watch can be adjusted
5. My old watch has a mode where you race vs your previous run. Not GW4
6. It loses my heart rate all the time when using 'Other workout'

One more thing, Samsung health app shows a graph of your workout with time on the X axis. However, you can't tell what exact minute and second the point on the graph refers to. It'd be great to be able to see that (needless to say, my 7 year old watch has that functionality).

I was thinking about returning the watch from the beginning but was trying to find solutions to those issues. Now my 30 days are over and it seems these are the worst 150 bucks I've ever spent. Samsung just seem to be a decade behind true sports watch companies. I'll try to get rid of this and get a Pilar/Fitbit/etc., I know those work as they are supposed to. I do NOT recommend this watch

title: Handy, good-looking, convenient.
text:
This is my first Amazfit product, so I cannot really comment on how well it works in comparison to other watches by the same manufacturer. But - it is affordable, looks very good, and works well out of the box. I was in need of a smart watch with a GPS tracker that would work with or without a mobile phone. This model checks all these boxes: the GPS works without a mobile phone nearby and seems very accurate. After completing a walking route that I know very well (and know the distance too), the GPS tracker measured my speed, distance walked, and mapped the walk very accurately (giving me the same numbers that I get by using my mobile phone GPS with apps like MapMyWalk or Strava). Its heart rate monitor is accurate too, but its oxygen (SpO2) meter seems to be inaccurate (I believe other reviewers also mentioned this).

Other observations: system updates are very quick (take about 2-3 minutes only). The Zepp app is reasonably easy to use and quite intuitive - one needs to go to "Profile" and then to "My Devices" (or "Add a Device") to add the watch and sync it with the app. Battery life appears to be quite good and the watch will keep charge for days. Charging is quick and takes about 1.5 to 2 hours (from the battery being down to 20% or below). The image is bright with vivid colors (becomes somewhat dim if the sun is strong) and the touch screen is responsive. The watch is very easy to use and there are plenty of options to cover many outdoor activities.

Overall - the Bit U Pro is among the most affordable GPS-enabled smart watches out there and, more importantly, it is well-made and offers lots of value.

title: Very useful info given; but move reminder isn't effective!
text: It took awhile to adjust to my new smart - fitness watch, but I love it! The only frustration is the "Get moving" reminder does not stay on the watch for long, so if you're not glued to viewing your watch, you'll miss it. In fact, I didn't think it was working at all: I used the online chat and eventually got a satisfactory reply. How it works is NOT described in the PDF manual or the online manual - which seems to describe everything else in detail. I wish it had that red line that showed when I wasn't moving. But it's a good sacrifice for all of the other useful information it tracks. I never thought I would actually read text messages on my watch, but I have found I do. I'm 65+ and try to keep up with technology. If you have an old Vivofit, you'll enjoy this. It uses the same app, but gives so much more info. I exercise 4+ times a week and can easily keep up with my heart rate by just turning my wrist - which also shows the level; you have to set your maximum rate... which uses the 5 level system developed in the 1970s -- REALLY!! That system has not really been proven effective scientifically, but it's been than nothing... I was concerned about the battery life, but it's really good. I just charge the phone when I'm showering... about 2/week.

All this comes at a cost, though. Battery life per charge is shorter, barely two days versus 3-pluf for the Active 2. title: Disappointing and infuriating
text:
My Fitbit Versa 2 was becoming wonky, so I took the advice of my local cellular store and got the Samsung Galaxy 4. It fails at counting steps and I can never get it to accurately log my elliptical workout. It counts less than half of the normal daily steps that my Fitbit did. Or I may find that as of 3pm, it has counted 40 steps. And it changes my settings, so I’m always fiddling with the app to fix. I have an Android, but not a Samsung, so some stuff, like ECG, doesn’t work. Wish I had just waited and switched everything to Apple - phone, watch, etc.

Update after 5 months, lowering to 1 star, will try to get a refund. I hate this watch The battery runs out and it goes blank with little notice. This is when it’s been charging all night, dead within 3 hours. I put it on the charger and it gives me a caution symbol which apparently doesn’t have a purpose other than to let you know something is wrong. I’ve researched and done everything possible to extend battery life. It may possibly be the extra charger I bought, they are reported to be picky about after market chargers. Then, the times I can get it to wake up, it says “charging paused” and I can’t get it off airplane mode! Oh, yeah, one of the “extend battery life” directions is to disable the continuous display, and also not have the “raise to wake” setting enabled. How about I just pull out my phone to check the time?
Lots of stories like this for this watch.
Thinking about replacing it with the cheapest, crappy plastic watch I can find at Target - just to have a reliable time piece on my wrist.
Update: why am I still fighting with this thing? Because it should work? To make sure it’s not user error?
I started charging only with the OEM cable to resolve those issues. That worked until today when I ran out of battery in mid-afternoon. What??!!
Then there are the repeated voicemail notices, long after I listened and deleted them all. And not connected to WiFi? Greyed out? Possibly needs a factory reset?
You know, I like tech. I work in tech. But that also gives me a short temper with stuff that’s unreliable. 😡

text:
Update: lowering to 3 stars. ALL the units need to be changeable to imperial and NOT default to metric for this watch to be useful in the USA!

Bought two. One for the ECG function for my husband but cannot get that function to work. The prompt reply with instructions from the manufacturer only measures the heart rate and does not apply to the ECG graph.
Good points: Love the GPS function for walking. Love changing the watch faces, just wish there were more serene or scenic choices. Love the sleep tracking.
Hiccups:
Blood glucose: what is mmol? OK I figured it out but what use is it if you want people to use it and not have to get out their calculators to decipher the results? My diabetic husband for sure will not use this “feature”.
Body temp: It is only manually entered and only in Celsius not Fahrenheit. It translates it to F on the chart after you enter in C. No option to select your preference under Profile/Settings/Units.
Walking: As I am walking it continually says "paused, restarted. Paused/restarted..." I don't miss a beat in my walking so not sure what the deal is but since it continues, I just deal with it for now...

So bottom-line; great watch for the price! Love the screen size. Easy to read in daylight. My previous tiny FitBit Inspire screen was invisible in daylight.

title: Worst customer service and warranty.
text:
Watched was a great product until it stopped working. Set it on the charger for about thirty minutes after it died. When I went to turn it back on the screen wouldn't come on, but I could tell it was on because it was vibrating for phone calls and messages. The backside looked like the battery leaked acid out.

Being only 8 months old Samsung told me it was still under warranty and sent me to a repair shop about 40 minutes away, who told me that they cannot repair watches, which Samsung knows but sends people to anyways, and I'd have to send it to Samsung.

The day Samsung received the watch they sent me a bill for $176 saying it was out of warranty. I called and they said it had liquid damage (if you google,many people have been told the same thing when it breaks) and was no longer powering on. The watch has never been in the shower or pool, only in rain which it is supposedly water resistant up to 200' of water. It also powered on before sending it to them.

I argued with them and Mikayla in the repair department said they would have a second person look into it and call back in 48 hours. 4 days later I recieved an email saying the watch was being returned unfixed and I never received a call back so I called and was told it was set for exchange. Talked to someone in the case management department and they said the price was going to be refunded. I asked how long and they said once the paperwork it accepted, then asked me to confirm my contact so they could START the paperwork. They never contacted me to start the paperwork, so I'm sure they were hoping I wouldn't call back and are still trying to stall. They told me to call back if I hadn't heard anything by Thursday, so I will be calling then.

title: Best fitness tracker for the money.
text:
This is a great fitness tracker. I got one for each of my preteen kids for an Easter gift. First of all, it was a huge hit; they love them. They love competing over step counts and what not and they enjoy diving into all of the fitness metrics. But the Bip U Pro is also a very capable fitness tracker for an adult.

I typically wear a Garmin Instinct and the BipU Pro compares very well to the Garmin. It is not quite as robust or as rugged/durable as the Instinct, but it is every bit as capable in terms of tracking workouts, sleep, heart rate, etc...
I wore my Instinct on one wrist and the Bip U Pro on the other to compare them on a few workouts (swimming, jogging, biking) and they were nearly exactly the same. In fact the Bip U Pro seemed to be a couple of seconds quicker with my heart rate readings.

Now it's really just a fitness tracker; not really a smartwatch. If you keep that in mind, a less than $70, you will not be disappointed.

Charging is difficult. Even though the contacts are all very clean, the connection is very touchy. Sometimes it doesn't charge.

Sometimes this watch goes totally black for hours as if it's bricked and then suddenly things are normal and the display comes back up.

PulseOx is nearly worthless and was lousy from day 1. It's frequently 10% or more off from a good calibrated pulse ox at my doctor's office (we've compared them).

The sleep tracking is kinda useless too. It cannot tell if you're taking a nap or not, and only starts tracking sleep during the hours you preset it to that's your normal schedule. It pretends to know if you're in deep sleep, light sleep, or REM but in reality these end up being merely wildass guesses.

title: THE BEST Smartwatch out there with GPS & OTHER Great Features for the Buck!
text:
I love Amazfit Watches. I've tried many other brands of smart watches, but I must admit, that Amazfit offers the BEST watch, with the most useful features - for far less than other Smart Watch manufacturers. I was using the Amazfit Bip S watch as my daily Smartwatch and thought that I couldn't find a better watch. Then, Amazfit came out with the BIP U PRO! The BIP U PRO is truly a winner 🥇! Slightly larger screen, gorgeous screen, plenty of beautiful and totally free watch faces, 7 to 8 day battery 🔋 life before recharging, built in GPS, ALEXA (with Mic) in the watch - that will interface with your cellphone and show you instant info from Alexa on your BIP U PRO SCREEN. This watch has so many useful features: Accurate Fitness Tracker with over 60bFitness Activities , Heart Rate Monitor, Blood Oxygen, Sleep Monitor. The other 2 cool really useful features are: Music Control (Control the music volume, and skip tracks - from your Amazfit BIP U PRO - that is playing through your cellphone) and Camera Control (Push the screen on your BIP U PRO) to snap a photo on your cellphone - great for a group photo shot (where your cellphone is clamped in a tripod) and you get to be included in the photo.
Amazfit has really upped their GAME with the BIP U PRO. I challenge you to find ANY Smartwatch on the planet for $70.00 with built in GPS and Alexa, a gorgeous screen that lasts 6-8 days and all of the other amazing features. You simply CANNOT!
Just buy it, and you'll never be sorry!
I have given 3 of these watches to family members and they were all greatly appreciated.

=====================================
UPDATE on 2 of my BIP-U PRO Watches - 8-9-2021
=====================================

1 of my Amazfit Bip U Pro watches developed a crack in the screen in under 3 months.
I have contacted Amazfit support to see how they will respond.

I bought a 2nd Amazfit Bip U Pro watch -- to replace my cracked one -- in April, 2021 and the new watch decided that it wants to STOP counting my steps at around 1600 or 1800 Steps - after 4.5 months! The screen will just freeze at 1600 or 100 steps taken. Even after a full factory reset and re-loading the firmware --- the same problem of my steps freezing at 1600 or 1800 steps. I cannot wear this watch any longer -- because it is totally inaccurate.

I am currently awaiting feedback from Amazfit Support on these 2 watches.

I am currently using my original & trusty: AMAZFIT Bip-S --- that truly I Iove and have never had any issues with!

text:
When buying a smartwatch there's three things I look at:

1. Does it look good? - I bought the black 40mm version and it looks slick. The black rubber wristband is comfortable and didn't irritate my skin when sweating.

2. How's the battery life? - Obviously this depends upon use and connectivity. I have everything off (wifi, location, HR tracking, etc.) except for Bluetooth so that I can receive work notifications. For 8 hours of Bluetooth it uses about 35%-40% of the battery. Whenever you have a phone call or play media on your phone, the watch will sync and drain the battery faster.

3. Does it have the functions I want/need? - For me, yes. I just need a good looking watch that connects to my phone and has its own location for tracking my bike rides.

title: A Good Intro Fitness Tracker (B rating) *Not a Smart Watch*
text:
I have been using this fitness tracker watch for about a month now and I give it a B rating for quality and function. It gets about 7 days of use before I need to charge it and easily synch with my iPhone for recording data/updates. The silicone band is comfortable and doesn't cause me irritation or noticeable as I wear it all day. The waterproof is good for showering, swimming, and I have free dove down to about 20 ft with no problems or issues. I am 6'2" and about 220 lbs and it fits my wrist just fine,

Issues:
- The watch face scratches very easily (get a screen protector)
- If your arm isn't moving it won't count steps. (Hands in pockets or pushing a shopping cart equals no steps)
-I have been standing at my desk for a half-hour, walking around the office, and the watch will say I need to stand and move around.
- Display is hard to read with some of the face options. Whish I could customize the things to show and were on the screen.
- Limited and weird activity options for working out. 3/4 of the activities aren't anything that I will use.

What I like:
- Battery life is good but GPS will drain it faster when bike riding, running, or other sports.
- Easy to use menus and synch with iPhone.
- GPS seems to be accurate and works in a variety of locations with coats and gloves.
- Lightweight and comfortable
- PAI, Blood Pressure, O2 are accurate.

title: Love this watch especially because it's water proof
Good watch....affordable price
text:
My Fossil 5 Generation Smartwatch started giving charging problems so I decided to get a new smartwatch.
After doing some research online I decided to get the Amazfit Bip U Pro……… This Amazfit Bip U Pro. has a very sleek design with a minimal and lightweight feel, weighing only 31 grams, plus a large and bright screen for the price.

The face of the watch measures 3.63cm and is rectangular in form. The screen doesn’t take up the whole face, there is a bezel around the whole edge of the watch.
The whole body is made up of polycarbonate and is built well and the display is protected with curved Corning Gorilla Glass 3 for additional protection.
This watch shines when it comes to fitness and health-related features with the inclusion of heart rate, SpO2, sleep, breathing tracking and much more. It comes with a host of workout modes, including running, swimming, cycling, elliptical training and walking.
You can navigate the watch by either using the button on the right-hand side or by swiping through it on the touchscreen.
Setting up the Amazfit Bip U Pro is a snap. After removing it from the box turn on the watch, and the face displays a QR. Capture with your phone’s camera. The Zepp app automatically began downloading and then sync with your phone and watch via Bluetooth it takes less than 10 minutes.
I particularly like the following features:

1. Notification of incoming calls, text messages, apps, calendars, alarm clock, weather forecasts, and
2. Support controlling the music and camera of your smartphone.
3. The heart rate monitoring feature appears to be accurate.
4. The fact that it is water-resistant up to 50 metres,
5. It has s a Pedometer

This budget smartwatch also comes with several great features including built-in GPS for outdoor tracking and a voice assistant with Amazon Alexa integration. In fact, it’s one of few budget watches to have GPS.
So far, this watch has lived up to my expectations so far, I have no regrets about purchasing this Amazfit Bip U Pro
If you’re looking for an affordable fitness tracker with a good battery at an affordable price, then the Amazfit Bip U Pro is the one for you.

title: A good watch with a terrible OS - I strongly recommend not buying it...
text:
I have used Samsung Active 2 and Samsung Watch 3, so my review is a comparison to those watches.
All the good things in this watch are what comes from Samsung. All the bad things come from moving away from the Tizen operating system towards the new OS. Here are the things I hate about this watch:
- Terrible battery life -- both Samsung active 2 and watch 3 have a better battery life, since this is supposed to have a large battery I can only assume the new OS is a battery hog.
- Lack of free watch faces - Tizen OS provides hundreds of amazing watch faces for free from independent developers. Comparatively we are in a desert landscape on this OS. All watch-faces want to sell you the features. App store does not help you find the free faces, instead is pushing the super expensive watch faces (think $200 for absolute crap). You can buy subscriptions for apps that allow you select from different watch faces, but they change you just to remove the ads that make the app unusable, and then charge you for the watch faces. What a joke.
- Google play store design for Watch apps is terrible and confusing. Samsung wear app has an amazing marketplace for watch apps, but for this watch it sends you to Google play store.
This will be my last Samsung watch unless they fix a lot of these issues. I find myself going back to Samsung Active 2 and Samsung Watch 3, both superior watches to this watch. I recommend you find those on sale and buy them. They are 100x better than this watch. I hope that Samsung allows us to install the Tizen OS on it so we can salvage some value out of this watch.

title: Athletic Peeps, Beware! Body Fat Monitoring Very Skewed
text:
#1: Battery Life
I'll be frank: the battery life sucks (but we all probably expected that going in -- no one tries to hide it. The battery doesn't last a full 24-hours...which means unless you're absolutely stationary for about an hour out of each day when the watch is charging, you're not going to get a totally precise accounting of your steps.

#2: Body Fat Percentage
If you're more active than the average bear, it's going to be completely off. If you fall into the average category in terms of body composition and activity level, it would probably be more accurate. Where this became especially disappointing is that the app doesn't allow the user to enter anything more than height and weight as the metrics used as a basis for calculating the user's body fat in conjunction with the electrical impedance; I expected there to be a feature (similar to my body fat monitoring scale) in which one could enter one's activity levels, or even have the option of switching to "athlete" mode...but Samsung didn't make any such provisions.

...Since there's a lot of controversy around body fat monitoring in general, let me provide some more concrete data from which you can extrapolate the extent to which you're willing to put any weight on (pun intended) Samsung's body fat monitoring...

I'm a 5'4" female, age 43; I weigh 113.5 pounds. I work out 2.5-3 hours per day 6 days per week. I'm vegan. Looking at me, most people estimate my weight as being about 10 pounds lighter than I actually am. My measurements are 32-23-34, and I wear an XS in most clothes. My body fat monitoring scale (set to "Athlete" mode) says (as of this morning) that I'm 8.5% body fat.

Samsung's body fat monitoring feature says I'm nearly obese at 28.0%.

Clearly something's off here.

While I don't entirely believe the 8.5% of my scale, I certainly don't believe what Samsung says. I don't even know where I'd put 28% body fat. I think the truth is somewhere between the two, and I'd estimate I'm actually around 15-18%.

10% margin of error between the two different devices seems about right.

So...if you're serious about your numbers, don't plan on relying on this gadget. Buy it for other reasons...

I purchased mine simply out of habit and to know that it would absolutely-positively be compatible with my Samsung S10 phone, which it is.

#4: EKG Monitoring

I've had Samsung fitness trackers for years. Usually I end up replacing it once every two years due to it suddenly going into technological seizures after having barely gotten it wet while doing dishes (no joke -- I can't swim and always take it off before showering, so there's really no excuse for that kind of shoddy performance in a gadget that's supposed to be used during light waterspouts). That being said, I've had the "Samsung Health" app for about 4 years now. For some reason, I can't access the newer EKG monitoring feature, yet it says the app is up to date. I haven't yet been able to locate a separate (or newer) app that Samsung is pointing to: the "Samsung Health Monitor" app. So essentially the EKG feature is unusable for me. This is unfortunate, as I have chronic health conditions that periodically make my heart rhythm get a bit wonky, and while I don't expect it to be 100% spot-on, it would be nice to get some kind of perspective when those moments occur.

#5: My Bose Noise Cancelling Headphones won't work now!

I didn't even try to add them to the list of devices the Watch4 communicates with -- it's just not necessary for my purposes (I'm never away from my phone, so I just listen to music on it instead of the watch). Nevertheless, after setting up the new Watch4, my Bose headphones won't work with anything other than my laptop. Not only that, but somehow it's hijacked (for lack of better words) the phone's internal speaker output, and nothing audible plays -- even when the headphones are turned off to the point of having shut down the Bluetooth connection. I'm sure there's a remedy, but I'm a little bitter about having to spend valuable time hunting down a solution, particularly when simply adding this new Watch4 opened a "door" that I didn't even ask it to open.

#6: Wristband (40mm) almost too big

If you've gotten this far, you've read my measurements. I'm petite. The last notch on the wristband of the 40mm Watch4 is loose; it doesn't flop down past my wristband, but my wristbone definitely keeps it in place. Not awful, but perhaps not ideal, either.

#7: Don't really notice it's there

The watch face takes up my entire wrist, yet I really don't notice its presence on my arm, which is a nice bonus.

#8: Sleep Tracking

Apparently, I don't snore. :-) I very much appreciate the improvement in the sleep tracking in that it now shows in no uncertain terms how much time is spent in "light" sleep, "deep" sleep, "REM" and "awake." Before, it simply showed a percentage of sleep efficiency and whether it was light or not.

#9: What its useful for (to me, at least):

No matter the so-called improvements, what I still find this watch useful for is quite basic: tracking steps, speed, pace (etc.) and monitoring heart rate and sleep. It appears fairly accurate for those purposes. That being said, I'm also a little bitter about paying $244 for this...particularly when I need to replace it every two years. But...it's helped tremendously to keep me on-track with my fitness goals, and for that reason and that reason alone, I'll probably never be without one.

text:
I have worn a bip smartwatch for years now, and had the opportunity to 'upgrade' to a bip U pro.
in many respects, they are identical. same band size, and can use the same covers/sleeves for the watch body.

BUT.

Pros:
--it is waterproof, unlike the original bip.
--it measures your blood oxygen level.
--it costs about the same for a bip U pro now as my old bip did when i bought that 3 years ago.
Cons:
--battery life is TERRIBLE compared to original bip. i was able to routinely get 3 weeks (or more) from a single charge on my old bip. it also lasted more than a month in a drawer without completely dying while i tested the bip U pro. I have NEVEr had the bip U pro last more than 10 days on a single charge.
--VERY limited choices for watch faces. i have yet to successfully install a 3rd party watchface.
--you have to use a different, new app, which does not seem to interface with the old app in any way.

basically, i traded waterproof for 2 weeks of battery life and a severe reduction in available watchfaces. not a great tradeoff, IMHO.

title: Be careful of the apps you install
text:
So as this is my first Galaxy watch I have decided to write an in-depth review to help people make an informed decision without having to go through the troubles that I went through purchasing my first Galaxy watch. To start off I looked at all of the Galaxy 4 watches and came to the determination that I wanted the classic style as the dial which is only available on the classic was what sold it for me. Now this is only my personal preference and does not take from any of the other Galaxy 4 watches. Prior to continuing this review I would like to say that my watch is a T-Mobile branded which may have different features then the unbranded model. That being said when I first received the watch the battery was dead. I charged it until the battery was full then went through the setup process. The process was very easy to set up on my Galaxy Note 10 plus. I cannot vouch for any other phone. One caveat was during the charge the watch had overheated twice and had to pause charging. I did not pay it any mind and figured that it had something to do with my 3 and 1/2 amp charger. So during setup it detected several apps that were on my phone and ask to install them to the watch. I did this. It also asked me to verify a number as it was pairing correctly you must do this on both the watch and the phone. After a short while it will finish the pairing and continue the installation process where you will have to select your plan and just basically finish setting up the phone this goes pretty quickly and is very easy to do for anyone. After the watch was completely set up I decided to install an app called facer which it's supposed to give you access to thousands of great watch faces. I did this and installed it exactly as it said and selected a watch face. So after this was done I setup my Microsoft Outlook and uploaded my contacts and all the rest of the stuff that I would need on this watch. I then wore the watch to work the next morning which I was completely upset about as the battery did not even last 4 hours. So after much troubleshooting I decided to do a complete factory reset of the watch Once I did this reset I started loading in apps as I had done the first time except I left out facer. This app appears to be the cause of the excess battery drain because instead of only getting 4 hours of use before the battery died I am now getting 12 hours and then it switches into a low power use mode basically watch only. Definitely not a deal-breaker. This watch contains quite a few very useful Health monitors to include a pulse oximeter, electrocardiogram, stress indicator, as well as all of the standard personal health things that you would expect in a Smartwatch or Fitness watch. It appears as though the band is replaceable if you want to replace it with a different style band. Replacing the band will not interfere with the watch functionality. The bezel along the face of the watch appears to be grooved along the bottom which allows for you to easily find the correct app that you want and lock it in place. This has two buttons along the side of the watch the bottom button is designed for going back a menu and the top one is set up primarily as your power button and Bixby button these two buttons can be programmed within the settings menu. Many of the built-in Samsung watch faces are customizable meaning that you can change the colors and change what apps open and what is tracked. This does use the Samsung 1 u i as its primary however Google has granted Samsung rights to the wear OS that being said this is a custom operating system strictly for the Galaxy watch 4. It is the wear OS! That being said almost everything that is designed for the wear OS can be used within this watch. As I have not found anything yet that will not install into this watch I'm sure that there is something out there that won't install. One of the big features that I used quite a bit and this watch is the ability to use Samsung pay this works exactly like the phone where you just tap it to the pay terminal and the near field communication will do the work. You must have Samsung pay installed in your phone in order for this feature to work. You can make and receive phone calls on this watch and can also answer text messages which I thought was a great feature this does have GPS functionality and can be a controller for your phone's camera. A calculator that is located within the watch is a great idea however I found that the numbers are so small that it's near impossible 4 an adult to utilize this functionality accurately. It appears as though you can set alarms through this watch which I have not done yet. And this watch can also be used as a remote for multimedia apps installed on your phone. For example iHeartRadio can be controlled from your watch. This I find is a pretty decent feature. Now let's get on to the overall Aesthetics of the watch. So upon first use I want to say that this specific model of the Galaxy 4 watch has a very short band which barely fits around my wrist as I have played the guitar for years my wrist is very thick and bulky and the watch band is literally at the second to the last latching hole. Again not a deal-breaker but if you have larger wrist you may need to purchase a longer watch band. The watch band itself is very comfortable I barely notice it on my arm this does have a feature that is called a water lock. I am not 100% sure what this does so I can only speculate that it helps to try and push the water from The Watch after it has been submerged in water. I have not use this for sleep tracking yet I will test this at a later date and leaving update at the end of this review. As the bezel themes to protect of the watch glass for the most part it looks as though if you work in an area moving Freight like I do you could benefit by getting a protective outer case for the watch. I know there are few companies out there that make protective cases for these specific watches. After I purchase one I will write a review on it as well. So I have gotten asked on a couple of occasions is this worth the purchase or should I purchase the 46 mm. As the only basic difference is size and battery life. I would say that is entirely up to you. Now keep in mind, the 42 mm classic is quite a bit smaller then the 46 mm but they both function exactly the same. With me having fat fingers I can still use the 42 mm without any problems. So basically the price is increased in my opinion substantially for a little bit larger battery and a larger watch face. I would say in my honest opinion that it's not really worth it but it would come down to your personal preference. As of the date of this review I will go on record as saying that this is one of the best watches on the market and definitely the best watch that Samsung has ever produced. Granted it's still a little bit behind the Apple watch however if Samsung continues on the path that they are going this watch will become a direct major competitor with Apple and could overthrow apple as being the leader in smart watches.

So what is my take on this watch?
In a nutshell, this is a fantastic watch with a very sleek rounded design which could be worn by anyone for any occasion, it is classy yet reserved, sporty yet not overly so, and has all of the functionality and more then most of the fitness watches out there. The only thing I would like to see different with this watch is to have them add an actual charging block 2 the case. This has the USB charger, and this will charge wirelessly through your phone, but it did not come with a charging block. Again not a deal-breaker so out of a five star review I would give this a solid four star. If there is anything you would like to know about this smartwatch please ask and I will be glad to give you the info on it

Update..... so after using this for a few days I've noticed that there was several updates to the watch and with these updates it has also decreased battery life drastically. I'm not sure if there is an issue with the watch itself or if it's a problem with the firmware updates. But I will try and keep everyone posted as to what actually transpired with this. I will be checking with T-Mobile to see if they can find a solution and make the battery life much better. As of now I've had it off a charge since 6 a.m. and it is now 9:15 a.m. and it is gone from 100% charge down to 31% which in my eyes is 100% unacceptable.

Update2
So after much use and another factory reset I figured out that there are several applications on the Play Store that caused a significant battery drain on this watch. Once I removed the aftermarket applications from the watch I am now getting approximately 15 plus hours of battery life which is absolutely fantastic I have turned off some of the sensor features that I do not use which also increase the battery life. I am 100% happy with this purchase and this watch at this present time I will be purchasing the case for it had a later date as I would like to protect it although I don't feel that it does need protecting it does seem very durable. And I will be replacing the band eventually. Stay tuned for more updates.

Update number three
So this is my next update that I found which could be very helpful to anyone that is experiencing battery issues. Okay so what I found is that if you have an LTE version of this watch and your phone is not connected or within range of the watch it will switch to LTE mode which will drain your battery Ultra quickly as it seems to be scanning the network for any other type of signal other than LTE. To solve this issue simply either turn off mobile data for your watch or, make sure your phone is within range. I have been experiencing a massive battery drain issue since I purchased the watch and it seems to be very intermittent. Yesterday when I was at work I did not have my phone with me and only had my watch and that's when I noticed the battery drain was extremely intense it drained from 100% at 20 in a matter of about 3 1/2 to 4 hours. So I did an experiment this morning and was wondering if this indeed was the issue. I did find that the facer app is not an issue and it definitely was due to the LTE in the watch although, adding many apps will put a strain on your battery life I did not notice any type of significant battery depreciation after the facer app was reinstalled. Again I will continue to update as I find new things out but so far this watch I am finding is absolutely amazing. I would have expected that the LTE model especially if running off of Lte would be a little bit better but I will say that Samsung has improved drastically over their last set of watches.

title: Much better than my last smart watch.
text: I have written many reviews on many different products and as this is my first Galaxy watch 4 classic review. I am going to be as thorough and as honest and unbiased as I can be. So to start this off I want to start by saying that my watch was purchased from T-Mobile and is branded. This did come with a dead battery which literally after charging for approximately 10 minutes was that 30%.  During the charging I noticed that the battery was getting very very very hot which did draw a little bit of concern for me. When I finally turned on the watch it did automatically detect and download the app to my phone and started the setup process. It was relatively simple however it did appear to reset in the middle of setup which I do not have any clue why it did it and I had to redo the entire setup however, it did automatically detect my Mobile plan and asked me if I wanted to continue using that. The rest of the setup process was relatively easy. I did notice that during the initial setup process it did reduce battery life drastically as I went from a full 100% down to 50%. I don't know if this is due to the battery or if this is just a one-time thing. I will update this periodically as I find more information regarding it. The watch face for the 42 is pretty decent sized however the band length is kind of on the small side for smaller wrists. I will be getting a longer band as this one barely fits around my wrist. Despite the short watch band I did notice it is very comfortable and barely notice it around my wrist the dial Around the Clock face is fantastic for people with larger hands like myself. It just makes it much easier to navigate the menus. When reading the menus it is extremely clear which I am quite impressed about as I have bad eyesight and have a difficult time reading stuff close up and I noticed that this I have absolutely no problem reading. Changing watch faces is very easy and there are thousands to choose from in fact there are apps that will allow you to create your own which is a benefit as it will make it very personalized to you. As I cannot touch on battery life at this moment I will update this in the future to include the overall battery life. As of this day it appears that the battery does last quite a long time considering the size of it. However this will vary based on graphics and or animation and how frequently you use it. The watch Face Screen does have a automatic off and it does have a low power cut off which automatically activates the time mode only. So you will still have access to basic watch functionality if you get extremely low on battery. The plus side is that the battery charges relatively quick from empty too full approximately three hours. Of course this depends on the charger speed obviously a 3 amp charger is going to charge faster than a 1/2 amp charger. The charger I used was a 3 amp rapid charge charger. Some of the apps require the installation of Samsung and or T-Mobile apps for example do you sleep tracking and electrocardiogram require Samsung Health to be installed on your phone and it does have a watch based app with it. Although I have briefly used this it does appear to work pretty decently although I have not compared it to an actual electrocardiogram I can visualize actual patterns. And it does allow you to review these patterns at a later time so this could be good as a self-monitoring device of course it's not to be used in place of an electrocardiogram which is ten thousand times more accurate. It does appear that this is a Samsung specific wear OS app maybe a branded alteration of the wear OS however it is definitely wear OS. All of the teachers are exactly the same as the actual wear OS features with certain Samsung specific features. If you have a Samsung phone this streamlines certain processes. Especially during setup. As this is about all I have at this present moment I will update information as I find it relevant. I hope this review helps some people make an informed decision about this product. If there's any other information that you would like to know about feel free to ask and I will get that information posted quickly

title: I know from budget fitness watches. This is a good one.
text:
I've had quite the journey of fitness tracker watches. From a Samsung Active2 (premium features, but way too heavy and bulky, and gave me a rash) down to a Mi Band 6 (adequate features and comfortable, but too small to read easily). I've learned that if you're looking to save money, it's a game of acceptable compromises.

I feel like the Bip U Pro might be a nearly perfect balance on a budget.

Pros:
* Bright, sharp responsive screen. Seems to be right in the sweet spot of big enough to read easily, small enough to not look ridiculous (and cheap) on your wrist (see below in the cons, though)
* Customizable menu screens (to a degree -- see cons)
* Easy-to-use Zepp app for setup and activity tracking
* Smooth integration with phone music players (including Pandora)
* Notifications work perfectly (as a subscript to this, this watch is even smart enough to delete read messages from the watch automatically. Not every watch has figured this out)
* DND (do not disturb) works perfectly (wish every watch got this right. Even Samsung mysteriously crippled theirs)
* Offline to-do list! I've wasted more time trying to find work-arounds for this on every other watch I've owned (even Samsung). Amazfit puts it right there on the front page!
* Instant syncing. The Mi Band required a human sacrifice to sync. Every. Single. Time.
* Pomodoro tracker! Didn't know I needed this until I found it on the Mi Band. Now can't live without it
* SpO2, heart rate, sleep tracking, all that good stuff. Seem reasonably accurate, but I don't put huge faith in devices at this price point being medical-grade equipment
* Alexa support! It has a built-in mic (but just like everything Alexa, this only gets you so far. Some things are just quicker and easier to do yourself)
* The Pro also has a built-in GPS, although it's still winter so I haven't had a chance to try it out
* Looks a lot like an Apple watch :)

Cons
* The screen looks nice, but it's weird that it doesn't use the full real estate of the glass. There's a bezel around the edges that takes up about 1/4 of it. Not a deal breaker though
* Wish "lift wrist to wake" was more sensitive. Failing that, a "tap to wake" would have made up for this
* No automatic workout detection that I can find. An odd choice for a fitness tracker
* No way to customize the workout screen to show only your favorites. An acceptable work-around I found is that the screen does display most recent activities first, so if you only do a couple of sports regularly you won't have to dig through the list every time
* No, you can't answer messages directly from the watch. The Active2 is the only watch I've owned that could do this, at of course a premium price
* Can't install additional apps. Again, have only found this on Samsung
* Limited selection of faces, but then I don't want to spend a bunch of time looking for a new one

It's early days, so let's hope this doesn't suddenly start giving me a rash (it took the Samsung a few months before I had problems). I'll update if anything major happens to change my opinion. As of this writing though, I think there's a lot of device for the price here!

title: Works like it should, it's just a bit big for my taste
text:
I was very hesitant to buy this watch because I was scared it would break on vacation and it was kind of big for my taste. I did so much research and asked many people who already had it and those who had different watches what they liked and didn't. I basically wanted a small waterproof smartwatch because I was going on vacation and was going to be in the water, both pool and sea, for a few weeks and would actually be in the water about 6 hours a day. I wanted to make sure this would not get water logged, overheat or have battery drain. I was very impressed.

1. WATERPROOF - I did use the water block feature when I was actually in the water and it worked great. It tracked my activity correctly and logged all of my physical data. I was able to access most functions with water block on, obviously not some of the notifications, but the basic features worked well.

2. OVERHEATING- When I was out of the water, and had water block off, it worked great, I was also in the direct sun for about 6-7 hours a day and worried it would overheat like a cell phone but it didn't at all. I was in temperatures around 90° and over for 6+ hours a day in full sun and it did not overheat or even feel hot or slow down. I did take care to keep my arm in the shade tho, when possible, I wasn't looking to break it.

3. BATTERY DRAIN- I did not have any issues with battery drain at all. I did charge it every night, but that was just out of force of habit because I'd charge my phone every night too and both chargers were on my nightstand. The battery at night was always over 80% regardless of how much I accessed the features during the day. I used notifications, fitness, timers, reminders, email, and others. I traveled with it on for 19 hours straight and was in 4 different international time zones and it still had about 70% charge when I got back home.

For me personally, the face it too big. That's just personal preference though. I understand you cannot make a watch with all the capabilities this one has with a tiny face. I personally prefer a watch to actually look like a watch and not a smartwatch, I wanted something that I could wear and have it look like a real watch. Knowing I'd have to sacrifice a quality and features to get that, I decided to buy this instead. I do not regret it. It's a durable and very functional watch.

title: Improved! Latest Firware update fixed the major issues I had.
text:
The latest firmware update has fixed all the issues I had with this watch (R870XX...M1EVB4 circa Feb 25th, 2022). I have been using the new firmware and started wearing my watch 24/7. I just charge it while showering now, so the battery usage has been greatly improved. It is also checking my pulse rate and oxygen levels at night without draining it to nothing. To top it off, the elliptical interface now actually counts my steps on the elliptical! Thus I am MUCH happier with this watch than a month ago. They did not break the good stuff and improved all the broken stuff (that I cared about anyway...).

--- ORIGINAL REVIEW (2 stars) ------------------
Samsung has always made good stuff, and sometimes really good stuff. This watch is NOT it. I bouhgt it primarily for tracking my activity, which is STINKS at. I use an elliptical and it successfully figures out I am using one, tracks the calories used and time on the thing, but gives me ZERO steps. Really hard to compete with my wife's steps when I get nothing for 45 minutes on the elliptical. Then there is the battery life issue, it has none. If you want to use it to track your sleep and maybe keep track of your oxygen level, etc, then it will empty the watch every day and then you have 2 to 3 hours to charge it back up, therefore I took to trying to charge it while I am at the computer. Well, that does not work out well because I keep forgetting to put it back on. After 50 years of wearing a watch, I don't want to be taking it off in the middle of the day when I usually need it. So, I just don't wear it at night and gave up on the sleep tracking function, and let it charge overnight.

As for functionality, that is all pretty slick. The apps work, the watch faces have enough choices for me, being able to connect over various apps seems cool and works - after a fashion - if you don't mind your battery power draining to nothing pretty fast. So, I like my old tracker from their competition much better. I could where it all day and night and track everything and it charged up completely while I was in the shower. It just was not very durable, and they kept breaking, so wanted to try Samsung. sorry I did.

Oh, and I submitted a trouble ticket 3 weeks ago... Still no response. An update just downloaded, will update this if it managed to fix anything, but I doubt they can do anything about the absurdly slow charging and absurdly fast discharging.

so to summarize - the smart watch can do everything you want a smart watch to do, it does it well, just not for very long... So kinda useless if you ask me.

title: Upgrade from Active2?
text:
I am a fan of smart watches, over the years I have had a Pebble, then a progression of Samsungs-- Gear Fit, Gear Fit Pro, Gear Sport, and Active2. Before smart watches I was a collector of mid-tier mechanical watches, attracted to watch faces that I liked. (Looking at you Lum-Tec!).

Smart watches did not attract me for fitness tracking, but rather for the multitude of available watch faces. Truth be told, I do like the form factor of apple watches, but the 24-hour battery life and needing an iphone are reasons I originally decided to steer towards Samsung. My primary uses are for call / text notifications, Ring door alarms, exercise and sleep monitors, and timers/alarms. Much has been written about Samsung watches, and based on Amazon comments there seems to be a love-hate relationship with the Watch 4, so I am just going to limit my comments to a couple of points.

First, battery life. I was happy with the Active2. Battery life with both the prior Active2 and this new Galaxy Watch 4 is OK, not great, for me, usually 2-3 days...The initial setup scheme, unlike the Active2, showed less than 24 hours use from 100 to 12%--so I understand where "poor battery" comments come from. Over time and charging cycles, dependent on the selected watch face, along with power saving tips, I can get a solid 3 days.

Power saving tips. AOD “Always on” needs to be OFF, display set to 10 seconds, wrist flick screen OFF, HR measurements set to every 10 minutes except during daily exercise sessions, snore detection and blood oxygen at night need to be OFF, Wireless OFF, NFT toggled OFF. I also found that some settings were set to off, but actually on (blood O2 at night, set to off, but running at night. I had to reset the watch?). Battery life could be much better, Samsung really needs to look at how they implement defaults that consume power considering the vast number of comments that complain about short battery life.

Second, initial setup. With the Samsung Gear app already installed on my pixel 4a 5G phone, set-up was easy with a switchover from my Active2. Most of my prior Active2 settings were carried over with the exception of NFT toggled back on, and a required update of the Samsung Health app to show my default exercises.

Third, a new marketplace. My most frustrating moment was the fact that previously purchased watch faces are not carried over due to the switch to Wear OS, and away from Tizen. Samsung Marketplace is no longer used for Watch 4. Oh well. There are plenty of options from google play (add watch face to searches) and from Facer. Be aware, increasing the number of complications, animations, and colorful backgrounds seems to noticeably hit battery life. As indicated, I have found a number of preset options that give me a solid 3 days of battery life, with the power saving hints above in play.

As for watch operation, it is all very familiar to me. I am learning the new operating system and menu. A positive surprise was a totally flat face allowing the use of glass screen protectors, very easily positioned and attached. The Active2 had a curved edge making the install of screen protectors more challenging and less durable along that same edge. I also like the design of the watch band, which sits mostly flush against the curved case, maybe following a styling cue from apple.

If, like me, you had a prior Samsung watch, this is technically an "upgrade"--but lots of adjustments need to be made to obtain good battery life, and some operational issues persist. With the current deal it might be worth a try. IMO, Samsung still has some firmware work to do.

title: Just as good as I expected
text:
What it does well:
- battery life and design are both great. The watch is comfortable to wear and a good size for smaller wrists. It's not very comfortable to sleep with, but I am not sure how that would be improved.
- This tracks calories burned, both active and your BMR (how many calories your body burns just by existing). It will automatically track some active calories burned, like from walking. To get the most accurate number, you'll want to use the activity tracker.
- The activity tracker is great but it took a bit to figure out how to get it to work. Hit the top button and select an activity you want to do (the activity list can be modified and reordered in the app), and it will start tracking. If you are doing strength training, you can use the bottom button to start/stop each set, and during your rest period it will show a timer to make sure you're resting properly. If you are using a treadmill, it will allow you to calibrate your distance at the end. I've found this is about 10-20% off of the actual distance so I will manually change it to whatever the treadmill displayed.

What it does not do well:
- Intensity Minutes. Just doesn't seem accurate at all to me.
- Sleep. Somewhat accurate, doesn't really tell me anything I don't already know.
- Tied to the "activity tracker" above, this doesn't actually record your sets very well. I am surprised the watch even does a decent job of this, so it's not a big deal to me, but I have to go into the app after every workout to input the correct number of sets and what the exercises are.
- no fees to use the app or full features of the watch!! looking at you fitbit, you greedy company

Couple interesting things:
- Body Battery. This tracks how much energy you've spent vs how much you slept. Could be useful.
- Stress levels. This just... confirms how stressed I am. Thanks?

Don't buy this if you don't plan on setting aside an hour or two to get all the settings worked out. It's worth the time because the watch provides valuable information if you're serious about fitness and optimization. I personally turned off ALL notifications to the watch because this is used for training and tracking, not another way to be distracted by technology. I turned off the activity reminder because if you have a desk job, it'll be buzzing at you ever hour or so to be active, and that just isn't practical or necessary at the level it takes to clear the notification.

title: How to avoid a watchband rash.
text: I saw a picture of a user who had developed a rash. Silicone watchbands can cause this trouble. The band is not allergenic but if pulled up too tight your wrist will start to sweat. If this happens, remove the watch for a few days to let the skin dry. Use some anti fungus skin cream such as Cortizon. When you put the watch back on, keep it loose fitting. This will allow your wrist to stay dry and the problem will go away. Make sure to keep the band a bit loose and the problem should stay away.

title: I've own 7 devices, 3 brands, love Polar but Garmin wins, here's why
text:
BRAND Comparison:
Fitbit – Pro: it is intuitive. Con: Micro-transactions. User is expected to pay monthly fees for services already on the device. Caters to Corporations rather than consumer.
Polar – Pro: accuracy in HR readings, offers arm band and chest strap combinations. Con: Expensive, zero customer service, Web and phone services cater to new models / Operating systems. Won’t play nice with older systems.
Garmin – Pro: does not charge extra monthly fees for features already on the device. If you don't like the hard band, there are hook and loop after-market bands that work well. The website and phone app works reasonably well with older software. Doesn’t offer an armband, BUT, the Polar arm band works when the sensor feature is turned on! Yes, you can use your Polar OH1 with your Garmin Venu Sq. Con: Garmin’s customer service is not as good as it once was. The live chat only works on some platforms.

Garmin Features
(Notice: There are more features, these are the ones I related to.)
Sleep
1. The sleep time goal cannot be adjusted. It is set to 8 hours and cannot be moved to more or less. Garmin has indicated they have no plans to change this.
2. The sleep readings are not very accurate. If one lays in bed after waking up and move their eyes around, the device will call it REM sleep...even if one is not sleeping. If one gets up to use the bathroom or let the pet in/out, the sleep reading may restart once sleep is resumed. (If one adjusts the sleep time to correct this issue, they will lose the Pulse Ox data, for the entire day if the all-day feature is turned on.)
3. The hours slept cannot be adjusted without screwing up the Pulse Ox readings, the Body Battery (energy) readings, and the Stress reduction readings. Seems they are all co-dependent on reaching that forced 8 hour goal. None will work well for those that sleep on their arm and may not work well for those that sleep on their side.
Weight Maintenance
1. Weight maintenance works in tandem with a third-party app called MyFitnessPal. (Good app but requires newer phone model to download.)
2. Using the Calories In/Out feature for weight control removes the total calories burn reporting from the phone app. Kind of annoying if one has a burn goal.
Calories
1. The calories report only gives weekly / monthly active calories. (Again if one has a daily burn goal, too bad for you.)
2. The daily, live, readings are good. It provides the total burn, then shows the breakdown of active and resting (non-active) totals. (It only does this if one is not working with weight control features.)
3. User can set calorie burn goals but the phone app does not respect them (keep reports on that goal.) User cannot set a daily burn goal.
Pulse Ox
1. This feature has issues related to the sleep feature.
2. The device offers a sleep only, all day automatic, and manual use.
3. Doesn't matter which you choose the device will default to average readings or last reading at times. 4. Turing off the sleep readings while leaving on the all-day readings will result in no posting of all day readings. You can see them on the device but not on the apps. Turning off the automatic reads (both sleep and all day,) one can still manually read, and these numbers (accurate or not) will report to the app.
Respiration
1. Works during sleep regardless of the Pulse Ox setting.
2. If one uses the breathing feature to relax, some strange readings may occur. For me, using the relax feature decreases the reported count to 3 breaths per minute and increases the stress.
3. Respiration rate does not appear to report during exercise. (I find this annoying.)
Heart Rate
1. Is reasonably accurate when compared to other brands and other devices.
2. Keeping the wrist band high on the wrist is required to gain accurate readings. Not comfortable but functional.
3. Resting rate is not a resting rate. It is the daily low. There doesn’t seem to be a feature of actual taking of resting heart rate.
4. Low, high, and current (live) rates are available on the phone app. The device reads the heart rate about every 5 minutes or when activity is detected (this feature can be changed.)
5. If the device is set to read real time, a notice suggests the battery could be drained faster. I use that option and charge every two to three days with activity.
6. The customization of the device (some of which are downloaded separately) provide many options for seeing this data during a workout.
Body Battery
1. The body energy feature is not functional in my opinion. It is tightly related to sleep hours, patterns, readings. If the user has different sleep metrics then the device, they will find their energy level does not recharge even if one feels they’ve had a good sleep.
2. The body battery drains all day during activity. If one wants to recharge (relax,) the move feature will harass them to get up and move, which results in more drain. Not a good feature; it can be removed or ignored.
Stress
1. The stress feature is also based on the unfortunate sleep feature. Movement causes stress, not moving causes the move feature to harass. It’s stressful on its own. (stress feature can be removed or ignored.)
2. Using the option to de-stress by included programs caused me more stress so that didn’t work well.
Other
1. The option to download widgets, apps, faces, is great. Not every item is good but the selection and options are.
2. Faces included are customizable. (Includes both analog and digital faces.)
3. Nice face appearances and data selections are included, but the information doesn’t talk about this so take a look before hunting for a new face.
4. Features are mostly customizable. (User is not forced to look at golf apps / widgets if they don’t golf.) Remove the ones you won’t use, keep the ones you will. Space is limited so choose wisely.
5. If a featured item is removed, it can be reinstalled.
