THE GOOD: It is by far the most accurate fitness tracker that I have ever owned (four) - even one that I had previously payed $200 for. Heart rate, steps, calories (etc) are spot on. The sleep monitor is spot on. It matches my CPAP sleeping machine wink-for-wink. The GPS is good, but not great. The phone sync is adequate; it picks up calls and texts just fine. The band is comfortable and does not pinch if you adjust it correctly.

THE BAD: The Amazonfit app is now "ZEPP". The instructions are sparse. It is very hard to figure out, and even when you do, the navigation is tedious. The watch I have froze up on me once and I had to do a factory reset. After I reset, not only did I lose all of my workout data on the watch, I lost all my data on the app on my smartphone. I still have not yet figured out how to use the music function to act as the control for my phone, even though I use Amazon Music as my platform

THE UGLY: The battery... No other way to say it - abysmal. Not only does it last for only four days or less, it takes almost two hours to charge if watch is under 10%.

BOTTOM LINE: If you can live with what I have experienced for the last four months, then this is the best fitness watch for money. The "bells and whistles" that the more experience watches promise are simply overrated.

title: Lasts 1 day, Good data but no guidance
text:
I'm pretty disappointed in this Garmin watch. I researched for over a month because I wanted better quality data for my health. I decided to go with this watch because it shares the same sensor as the more expensive models at a fair price.

I had the Mi Band 5 before this and was very happy with it aside from the stress tracking and horribly inaccurate fitness tracking when lifting weights (did fine with other exercises). So I bought this watch, the new Index S2 Scale (definitely don't recommend) and the HRM Pro Chest Strap (wonderful) to use as a system. Overall i'm ****ed!

This watch lasts a whopping 1 day and I have to leave it on a charger for about an hour or more it seems. So I have daily chunks of data missing every. single. day. My Mi Band 5, which only cost $34, would last 4/5 days. Granted this watch has an O2 sensor which has been nice but 1 day of battery life is RIDICULOUS! Garmin forums recommend to turn off the O2 sensor and reduce the tracking, but why in the world would I do that if that's the reason I bought the watch in the first place?

I will say Garmin does a great job tracking data that can help your health but they offer NO GUIDANCE whatsoever. In example, you can see your pulse and respiration rate but you have NO CLUE whether it's in a good range or not. And if it is, there are NO SUGGESTIONS on what to do about it. My cheap Mi Band 5 would show you what was normal, what wasn't and things you could do to improve that particular health metric. The fitness goals are USELESS. The American Heart Association suggests 200 minutes of activity? That's garbage, I do that in 1.5 workouts. My Mi Band 5 would use a much more refined and sophisticated "PI Score" which was exponentially better and tailored to the individuals resting heart rate and other health factors. That's a band that cost 1/6 what this watch cost me.

I'm astounded that a foreign company did such a better job when it comes to improving health vs what Garmin does. They're one of the leaders when it comes to health tracking but offer no guidance in their app on any of their metrics, I'm dumbfounded.

I do like the fact I can track my sets and rest time between sets as well as view my pulse while working out. The HRM Pro paired perfectly to my watch and syncs beautifully! This is probably the one and only thing that I really love about this watch. I'd say if you're really trying to do something for your health, save your money and get a Mi Band 5 with their Smart Scale. You disappoint me Garmin.

title: Most of the features do not work
text:
I bought this watch primarily to keep track of my heart rate without having to use my pulse oximeter. The watch consistently shows that my heart rate is ten beats higher than what my pulse oximeter says. My pulse oximeter works and is accurate and I've compared it to readings at my doctor's office and the hospital. I set up vibrating alerts for low and high heart rate. My heart can go to under 50bpm and as high as 160bpm. I set the alert for under 60bpm and higher than 110bpm. My heart has definitely reached the low end and high end of the spectrum and I haven't received any alerts.

The oxygen saturation detection does not work. It is consistently 10-20 percentage points below what my pulse oximeter says.

The fall detection does not work whatsoever. I have fallen several times while wearing my watch even after I toggled the option to be more sensitive to falls. It did alert me of a "fall" when I was slapping my leg to get my dog to come to me, but when I've fallen really hard, the fall alert has not come up.

I am a small person, meaning my wrists are also small. They measure 5.25" around. The small watch band is too big even on the smallest setting. Also, because of the way the band folds under the watch, it makes the watch not sit completely flat. One side is slightly raised. I can easily fit two fingers under the band.

The sleep tracker is not accurate. It has said I'm awake when I am most definitely asleep and vice versa.

The pedometer feature does not work. It counts steps when I'm literally doing yoga on the ground.

Overall, this watch was a complete waste of money. I would advise anyone to get an iPhone and then get an Apple watch. Samsung missed the mark entirely.

I generally put the watch on the charger after my evening walk and then put it back on before going to sleep. This allows it to start at 100% charge each night. Texts and phone calls can be accomplished on the watch, but I pull the phone out for these.

I did purchase a health synch app to get my sleep and workout data from Samsung to Google Fit. The app cost about $3 as a one-time purchase and has worked perfectly so far. title: Spot-On Performance? Nah, but Still OK
text:
If you are the kind of person who would become incensed that a device recorded two steps when you took five, buy something else.

Keep in mind that hospitals do not slap a fitness tracker device on your wrist to measure heart rate, pulse ox, et cetera. This device will give you basic health information, but it is never going to be as precise as devices that attach in other spots. It will never be spot on with its performance data.

The pulse ox measurement is not accurate at all. Sleep tracking is suspicious to me because the numbers change throughout the day, and no one can tell me why. Overall, though, if you go into this with the mindset that the device is providing general (and not spot on) data, you won't be disappointed.

The device is comfortable enough to wear all day and at night. It provides good enough data for my purposes. I am not and have zero intentions of ever being an elite athlete. I just wanted basic info that was "close enough" to accurate. If I want more precise data, I can hook up a pulse oximeter to my finger or slap on a blood pressure cuff. For your average use, it's just fine, especially at this price point.

So - unless you really, really need spot-on accuracy, this device is fine.

Also - look closely at these reviews. For some inexplicable reason, Amazon puts reviews of the Venu Sq product on the page for the Venu product. Garmin makes two devices - Venu and Venu Sq. The price point and features of each product is widely different, so pay attention.

P.S. I like this Venu Sq product much better than every Fitbit I have ever owned. It is much more comfortable. Having the interface on my phone is very convenient. I don't need a subscription for every data point. It's just a better product, IMO.

title: Affordable & feature rich smart watch
text: This was purchased as a gift for someone who's not really tech savvy. I have been a loyal Fitbit user for the past 7 years and currently own the Fitbit Sense which is the current top of the line Fitbit (I previously owned the Fitbit Versa). This Amazfit Bip U Pro surpringly has a lot of the same features as my Fitbit but at a fraction of the cost. I stay with Fitbit because most of my friends & coworkers use it so we can challenge each other and it's just easier to purchase accessories. Now back to the Amazfit... I like that you can take an SpO2 measurement anytime, unlike my Fitbit which only measures SpO2 at night when I'm sleeping and then it shows a reading. The Amazfit has other features that the Fitbit doesn't have such as a compass, way more activity tracking, it can control music from your phone and also act as a camera shutter for your phone. I like that you can create custom vibration patterns for your alerts (like for calls, texts, app notifications). The battery life is longer but that all depends on how your watch set up (screen time out length, vibration length, how often your heart rate is checked, etc). The one drawback for me with the Amazfit is that you cannot reply back to a text message or social media messages (not even with preset messages). You can reply with a preset message only when you get a phone call (you cannot answer a call from the watch or answer it until you get to your phone. It only gives you the option to silence, hang up or reply with text option). My Fitbit can reply to texts with preset messages or I can talk to text and reply that way which is wonderful. I can also answer my calls and talk through the Fitbit as long as my phone is within distance. If the Amazfit incorporated those features in the future, I may actually switch to Amazfit. I did see a more expensive version of the Amazfit at my local big box store so maybe in the future it will be more popular. I have heard good things about the Amazfit years ago but wasn't too keen on ordering something online without physically seeing or touching it in person. So when I saw a similar version at the store, I figured I'd give it a try and purchase it as a gift. The recipient loves the watch, it was purchased as a replacement smart watch so this one definitely has way more features (recipient previously used the iTouch Air SE and the screen became unresponsive to touch and the heart rate tracker stopped working). The Zepp app for the Amazfit isn't really too intuitive as many reviewers have mentioned but if you play around with it it's not too bad. I still prefer the Fitbit app better but if you've never had a smart watch before, you may not even notice a difference. I like that the Amazfit uses a standard watch band size so you don't necessarily have to order a replacement band marketed for the Amazfit. You just need to purchase the correct sized watch band. The Amazfit charges magnetically and you'll appreciate that the charging cord is fairly long especially compared to my Fitbit. The magnet only connects in one direction so there's no guessing if it attached correctly so you don't end up with an uncharged watch accidentally. The Amazfit is light and does feel cheaper than my Fitbit but maybe the more expensive Amazfit version is made with better materials (like not as much plastic). I do like the button on the Amazfit, it's much easier to press than the hepatic button on my Fitbit. As I mentioned before, I think the Amazfit is a good contender in the smart watch world. There are many models to compare depending on what features are more important to you. I would probably continue purchasing the Amazfit as gifts since it's much more affordable for all the features it comes with.

title: Amazing features for the pricepoint
text:
This is my first smartwatch. I came in with my eyes open after watching reviews and sifting through competitor's products, comparing and contrasting. I even made an excel spreadsheet of features, including the price as a barometer of what should be included. What can be hard to quantify is quality, beauty, and usability unless you've actually got your mitts on the product.

I am blown away. I thought for $169 I was going to get some half-baked fitbit clone, but this is not. This has an entire online ecosystem that you can use to leverage it's features. Yes, it has sleep tracking (which is not it's best feature), stress monitoring (which is nothing to write home about), body battery (which is quite good), heart rate monitoring (also quite good), and activity monitoring (which I think is its super-power). I think if you are not planning on using its activity tracking while doing some physical activity, this watch is not for you. There are other products out there like an android watch or something.

If you are looking for a relatively inexpensive health-tracking device that helps you maintain your exercise and weight, you have come to the right place. The Garmin ecosystem uses a mobile app called Garmin Connect which is indispensable to logging advancements and gains in your fitness regime. They also have an online version which is quite good that uses a customizable dashboard that you can setup to look over your statistics.

What I use everyday is the activity tracker which tells me my average heart rate, how many calories I burned, and if running how far I went. It keeps track of your records and congratulates you when you beat them.

A game-changer for me was when I started tracking my calories and hydration. The watch doesn't support inputting calories, but it has a "widget" you can download for hydration (which is not so good imo). What you can do is connect the Garmin Connect mobile app with a MyFitnessPal account, and easily track your calorie intake. I go into the mobile app and record my meals and water intake which helps me to balance my daily calories and hydration. I bought this watch recently and this has resulted in over 10 lbs weight loss.

There is tons of integration with your smartphone, notifications like SMS, emails, and anything else that plops on your phone screen gets ported over. The watch uses the phone to pull in data like weather and any settings you may have changed using the Garmin Connect app. One other thing to note is the Garmin IQ store. You can download apps, widgets, and watch faces, which make the watch much more cool than the default ones.

So, all in all there is a lot to offer and I am a proud owner of the Garmin Venu SQ.

title: This is a great watch but...
text:
I just bought this watch and owned it for about a week now. I'm quite impressed with all it's fancy features. I owned a galaxy watch s2 that came with my Galaxy S7 edge (pretty old now) back when I first got it. This is leaps and bounds from then. The other watch will last about a day or 2. This is watch is about 2-3 days if you use it here and there. Constant use will give you about 1-2 days. I don't use it for work, so I leave it at home because it will be ruined.

There are so many features of the watch. ECG which you could use as long as you're not pregnant or have a pacemaker. I just wish there was more information when using this mode as it's a bit too general for me. Watching your sleep patterns and how many hours and mins you slept is useful. Allowing your phone to be a microphone to naysayers to say they don't snore, could provide evidence if you do or not. Checking your stress levels (like on the galaxy phones of current and previous generations could), checking your heart rate, blood and oxygen levels, keeping track of your workouts. Especially if you go from running to treadmill, to weight machine, and circuit training, you could combine all those workouts into one by pausing the workout and selecting new and it will keep track of each exercise, your calories burned for that workout. Counting your steps as you walk throughout the day to find out how many miles, minutes you walked, how many calories burned for that.

Another cool thing that I've noticed is, changing the face watch so you never get bored with the same screen. Which is on every smart galaxy watch of previous generations but, also the ability to find your watch or phone (for finding your phone, you need to stay connected to your phone via bluetooth). Also there is a fall detection on the watch will alert you if you fall or had a car accident and if you don't dismiss the warning on screen it will alert the contact you chose. There are some air gestures to answer your watch, and some more features. That's all fine as long as you know that you will be charging your watch within a day or 2. For me, that's not that big of a deal as I conserve the battery as much as I could. Being that I don't use it for work and I should turn it off and keep it in one spot so it's easy to find. For those who are going to wear and use it at all times, you could choose to put it to watch only mode which isn't that great being that battery last about 24 hrs or less. title: Impossible to use.
text:
I REALLY wanted to like this watch, but sadly it looks like I'll be returning it after less than 24 hours.

The good: I have a small wrist and my previous low profile fitness band was discontinued (Jawbone). This thing fits great, the screen is small but not too small, and everything fits nicely with no gaps between it and my skin. Also love the green color.

The bad: almost everything.

First, the setup was so infuriating, I almost sent it back right then and there. It had to be updated in order to pair, for which you MUST scan a QR code from the watch's screen. Anyone see a problem with this? You're trying to take a picture of a bright computer screen with tons of tiny details. We had to get the lighting in the room JUST RIGHT, and as if that weren't bad enough, the watch screen kept timing out at the exact moment my camera could finally focus on it. I had to change the autofocus settings on my phone, and it still took forever! Something that should've been super easy turned into a two man job; one person to hold the phone and stay focused on the screen, another to keep the watch steady and press the button on the side every 2 seconds (I'm not exaggerating, we counted). The kicker? You can't change the screen settings until AFTER you update and pair it, so there was absolutely no way we could've made the screen wait longer to time out. It was ridiculous.

Screen issues seem to be a theme, because although the display is clear and colorful, it turns on and off at random intervals. I changed the settings so the screen would time out after 15 seconds instead, but this is completely meaningless. Sometimes it takes one or two seconds, sometimes longer, even if I'm actively touching it. It seems completely random and makes the watch itself almost impossible to interact with.

Then, when I'm not doing anything and it's locked, it will turn on all. the. time. I thought it might be reacting to movement but nope! I tried staying perfectly still and it continued to turn on randomly. And when I say random, I mean it. The same activity never makes the screen turn on twice in a row.

This wouldn't be so bad if I could just lock it with the side button, like my phone, and use only the app (something I'm used to doing with my old tracker anyways). But with the watch, "locking" doesn't turn the screen off, just makes it so you can't interact with the display. And it still turns on and off constantly.

So all throughout the night the screen is flashing on and off and I can't do anything about it. SUPER distracting and obnoxious.

Maybe I'm doing something wrong and there's a way to fix all this, but it's impossible to tell. The settings on the phone and watch are somehow both bare bones AND difficult to navigate (I can't even find where to change the temperature from Celsius to Fahrenheit) so it's impossible to troubleshoot. Plus, so far the watch seems to be ignoring the settings I change (like the screen timeout) anyways. Oh, and we even had to Google how to do that. This isn't a big name brand, so finding that info online took forever.

The manual is 10 pages long and only contains safety information.

I can't even comment on the accuracy of the metrics, because using this thing has been so difficult. It does things that don't make sense, it's impossible to navigate the settings, and everything is counter intuitive. The screen has a mind of its own, and let me tell you, that got old FAST.

This one fits so nicely, it really is tragic. I guess I'm getting one of the clunky fitness trackers with a huge screen or a bracelet that sticks out super far.

title: I'm probably not the ideal match for this watch
text:
First, ya'll need a place on your site with a more detailed tutorial of how to utlize each function. The short moving gif clips make it look so simple but then there's nowhere to go with your further questions for how to achieve the results you want.

Second, I had four issues to consider when choosing a smartwatch. To pay this much money for a device, it needs to meet all 4 needs.

1. I need an ECG. I use a little modular unit but I'd like to have one with me all the time.
I cannot get the ECG on this watch to work at all yet, even once. I've tried it dozens of times in dozens of positions. No matter how still I sit, it tells me I was moving or that my result was unreadable.

2. I need detailed sleep tracking. How long I'm in each cycle is important for my fatigue problem.
But I can't tell if it's accurate or not. It has lots of data showing up in the morning, but there are sleep and wake patterns that don't jive with my memory of the night before.

3. I need unlimited reminders, that are silent when I finally fall asleep. So far, they are very reliable even when I'm asleep (waking me up) or on another setting they don't buzz at all, just show up quietly on the watch.
Either the reminders can't be subdued by sleep or DND, or I just need to learn how to use them correctly. So far I haven't found that info online. I get that my alarm still needs to go off, but my entire to do list doesn't need to start buzzing when I'm trying to sleep in.

4. I have a child-sized wrist. Please make a watch small enough to fit on a wider range of people. Is petite people's money not good enough for ya? As it turns out, the 'small' band on its tightest notch is not holding the watch flat on my wrist when I rotate my forearms. It lifts up on one corner or the other. Not to mention it looks ridiculous and out of scale for small people. I have already begun the process of trying to switch bands out, but so far the aftermarket ones are longer, not shorter. Even the stretchy ones. But more are coming for me to test.

If the watch functions turn out to be not working merely because it can't get tight enough, I will return the watch but change the review up to 4 because my wrist is not your fault. But if I get a successfully tight band but it turns out you just sold me some functions that don't actually work, I'll return it and lower the rating to 2.

But I hope I just figure out how to get it to work for me, so I can give it a full 5 stars.

text: Overall this is a great smart watch for the price. You get a really long battery life depending on how often you prefer to track your heart rate and sleep; more tracking = 4 or 5 days, less tracking = 9 or 10 days. I've done both and decided to back off the tracking a little in order to only have to charge once a week. Charging is lightning-quick, usually about 30 minutes from a half full battery, approximately an hour from no charge to full. The various faces range from extremely useful to more like a traditional watch, with plenty of variety. Some of them can be edited to change what information is displayed. The PAI and GPS tracking is helpful. I like being able to rearrange menu choices so that my most-used functions are one menu level in, and those less used 2 levels in. Some don't get used at all, so I moved those off the watch. The Zepp application (why isn't it the amazfit app? or the Bip app?) works every time, no synch problems, serving up a ton of data in a fairly easy to understand format. Finally, I did encounter the skin discomfort, but finally figured out that this was my sweat drying and chafing under the band; it doesn't matter what band you use, you have to periodically wash (not rinse: WASH) the band and watch and then leave it off for a day or two to give your wrist a chance to recover. Make sure to wash your wrist & forearm too while you're at it. This watch is well worth the $60 I paid.

I am writing this review having never had a smart watch before (except 1 VERY BAD and CHEAP smartwatch, that lasted exactly 3 hours).

Setup took a LOT longer than I thought it would.

I also had to update my phone to be able to access the watch updating properly (I think it was 3 apps for the phone to be able to update the watch, which took an hour), then I had to download and install a few more apps for my phone to be able to mod the watch and locate it if stolen and get watch faces.

I think it took me 3 to 4 hours to get the watch, and my phone, totally updated to use (on my phone, I uninstalled anything I didnt need, or use, or want, long before getting this watch, so I had a LOT of apps to download and install from samsung just for my phone. If you have left your samsung phone with all the apps still on it and updated it all the time, then it will take you much less time than it took me).

I like EVERYTHING about this Watch 4, except 2 things:

1. Bixby. Piece of junk software that I dont need, dont want, and there is NO WAY to turn it off or get rid of the icon, or even disable it. I accidentally hit it 5 to 6 times in 2 days. Samsung, PLEASE at LEAST let us users be able to disable Bixby.

2. The band, or strap, or whatever its called. It would be great, IF it didnt make you put one side of the band UNDER the other side to lock it in. This pulls my arm hair, pinches my skin, and creates a bump under my wrist. Terrible, terrible design for a watch band. Its too bad too, because other than that, it is a comfortable watch band.

Other than those 2 issues, the watch is great.
After using it for a few days, and having Battery Saver on (which does 2 things. It makes the battery last for days. And, it also unfortunately disables a couple things I actually use, so I have to turn it off to use things I want, then turn it back on to save battery, which isnt as easy as it is on a phone).

The charge time is really, really fast (even during the 4 hour setup, which made the watch go down to 21%, it charged fully in just under 1/2 an hour).

I am disabled and have a lot of health issues, and I can use ECG and all the other health apps including sleep, during the day and night, and save the results to my phone which makes a chart for a month of all the results, which is a super feature, as I dont need multiple devices anymore, nor do I need to write results down anymore. To be honest, the ecg, bpm, pulseox, etc, is the main reason I bought the watch. And, the results are pretty close to what the Dr.s offices record, so its pretty accurate.

God forgive me, but I like being able to switch watch faces also. I wish samsung had a LOT more free watch faces, and I also wish they made it so that Ads dont play, but I love being able to go from stainless, to gold, to black, from analog to digital, to being able to actually customize where everything is displayed, and what I want to remove from being displayed. It is so much easier to look at my watch than to log into my phone to see the weather, or calander, or whatever.

Oh, and another thing I dont really care for, but is my fault, is the way to scroll. Never having had a smart watch before, let alone a samsung smart watch, I did not know that you scroll with the side of the screen. I keep launching apps I didnt mean to because of the scroll feature. I should have gotten the Watch 4 Classic, but I didnt know the wheel actually scrolled through everything until after I got the regular Watch 4. So, thats my bad, not samsungs fault.

I would definitely reccomend the Watch 4, especially for those with health issues. This is the best watch I have ever bought in my life. If you are an android samsung user, definitely pick one up.

title: Solid Performer: Inexpensive, Long Battery, Well Made - just don't expect It to be state of the art.
text:
I'm a long time Amazfit Bip (original) owner. Loved the original for it's always on display and super long battery life, and I do still prefer it to the Bib U Pro. But the U Pro is better in some ways.

I don't like that the U Pro doesn't have an always on display, but the display is much brighter and sharper so it is easier to read and better in bright light conditions. Battery life is longer then most modern smartwatches, but it's 6 days of real usage is far short of the originals 20+ real days. I would like to see a little for flexibility in turning off functions that I don't really use to increase battery life.

The new phone app is rather basic and simplistic, but does seem to be a little less buggy the original App.

Connectivity to my iPhone has been good and reliable, and much more reliable and faster then the original Bip.

The Bip U Pro provides all the information that I need, and provides much more then I want. But it does not have the advanced features of the newest (and far more expensive) Smart Watches.

Heart rate monitor seems reliable and fairly accurate. The pedometer seems to be more conservative in its counting compared to the original Bip, but I'm unsure if it is more or less accurate.

The U Pro is plastic and it looks a bit like an Apple Watch, but it seems robust and looks OK on the wrist. You DON'T need a screen protector or shield unless you want them. I used my old Bip for work outside and I never got a scratch on the screen and virtually no wear on the body after 3 years of use. The Bip U Pro seems to be just as rugged.

All in all, I recommend this watch if you want basic functionality such as heart rate, pedometer, and notifications and for it's relatively long batter life (once a week charging).

title: Short battery life, short band, no actually free watch faces
text:
After my Samsung Galaxy Watch Active 2 sustained water damage from less than a meter of fresh water, I had intended to purchase a Pixel Watch, Fitbit, or Garming smartwatch, but Amazon had a great deal on this 40mm Galaxy Watch 4 I couldn't turn down. I won't go into the positives too much, as there are numerous reviews talking about them, but it is far superior to the Active 2. The animations are smoother, the app compatibility is much greater due to using WearOS and not Tizen, the health features are better, and software support is until 2026. However, there are several negatives which I will list.

First is battery life, which is about 36 hours with the always on display set to off and a non-animated dark watch face. This is pathetic considering the Active 2 lasted over 2 days easily with the same settings. This means you will have to carry the charger with you everywhere if you are going on an overnight trip, as it is not QI compatible with all QI chargers, especially Anker brand.

Second is the watch faces. On previous Galaxy watches with Tizen OS there was a wide selection of free, nice watch faces. With the move to WearOS there are very few free watch faces, a good 99% have restrictions unless you pay, and due to the way WearOS treats watch faces, which are full-fledged apps, instead of just watch faces, app developers have access to much more of your data. Also, the number of included Samsung watch faces is few, even fewer than previous Galaxy watches. This negative will apply to all WearOS watches currently, however, but Samsung could have included a larger selection of first party watch faces considering the price of the watch. I will say that updates have added some new watch faces, like the Ball Watch Face, but it's not useful or desirable vs the kind of paid watch faces which have millions of downloads, and the Pixel Watch has many more included faces.

Third is the watch band. This version is for S/M wrists, not M/L wrists. This is not listed in the description.

If you can get this watch for under $140, and you don't mind charging it every day, and you don't mind using the included watch faces or paying for one, then you won't be disappointed.

title: Best Android smartwatch, with some minor issues
text:
I've used Samsung Galaxy watches since I bought the original Galaxy Watch in 2018. I bought the 42mm version because I don't like having a huge watch on my wrist, and the 42mm was still larger than any watch I had owned in the past. It had great battery life and I came to love the features, especially the alerts, ability to answer calls and respond to text messages, and the step/fitness tracking, even though I wasn't that active.

When the Watch 3 came out I decided to upgrade because it was a little thinner than the original watch, had ECG measurement, and still had all the features and apps I liked, including the physical bezel. I got the 41mm, which was the equivalent size to my original Galaxy Watch. It got a little less battery life, but I could still get at least 30 hours out of it, meaning I could use it all day, including for sleep tracking, and then charge it while getting ready in the morning.

When the Watch 4 came out I decided to upgrade because I liked the idea of using Wear OS and having BP measurement (if that is ever made available in the US). I decided to get the 42mm Watch 4 Classic, which was the equivalent to the Watch 3 version I already had. However, after using the smaller Watch 4 Classic for a little over a week, I found that the battery didn't even last 20 hours, and usually much less than that, even using the exact same features as on my Watch 3. As a result I sent it back.

Since the battery life was so bad on the smaller watch I decided to try out the larger version. However, after trying out the 46mm Watch 4 Classic side by side with the 44mm Watch 4 in a store, I decided that the larger Watch 4 Classic was just to large and heavy, especially for wearing for sleep tracking, so went with the 44mm Watch 4, to get the larger battery. That has turned out to work for me. With this version I can now get about the same battery life as on my smaller Watch 3. That allows me to wear it during the day and overnight and only charge it while showering in the morning. I'm finding as I get older I'm appreciating the readability of the larger screen vs. my earlier Galaxy Watches. Even though it uses Wear OS, the apps are essentially updated versions of the Tizen ones.

My only quibbles with this watch are the charging cable and the band. The charging cable that comes with this is just inconvenient. It's too short to use it with a charging cube in the wall and be able to place it on an end table or my desk. I could use it with my computer, but that's also less than convenient. I really preferred the charging dock that came with the original watch. It can be used with any USB cable, so I can use whatever length I need. Fortunately, I still have the charging dock from the first watch, and it seems to work with this one. I think Samsung should go back to that design.

I don't like the bands where the end tucks under the band, so I got the Samsung ridge sport band. While I like the look and feel of it, I don't like the extra curved part next to the watch on these. I makes the band stick out from the sides of the watch, making it seem larger than it already is. The watch is big enough without having the band make it look larger. My other issue with the band is the loops. Since the band is so smooth, the loops tend to slide down off the end of the band as I wear it. It would help if there were little tabs under the loops, or some other way, to keep them over the end of the band rather than slipping off. As a result I've replaced it with a Barton band.

Other potential issues with this are the fact that it only works with android phones. I have only ever used Android phones, mostly Samsung, so that doesn't matter to me, but if you're an Apple user this is NOT for you.

This also only has Bixby as a voice assistant. I never use voice control anyway, so that doesn't affect me, but Bixby is not great. Since this is a Wear OS device, they could add Google assistant to it, which would be better for a lot of people.

title: Unbeatable value, limited features keep it from being a distraction
text:
TL;DR: I bought the Bip U Pro for $60 about a month ago, and I've really enjoyed my first month wearing it and am glad that I bought it. It does everything I want it to and very little that I don't need it to.

The watch is very light, but still feels solidly built. The stock watch band is OK, but was cutting into my wrist a bit during extended wear, so I bought a nylon / velcro band for $8 and now I'm almost completely unaware I'm wearing it. The screen is bright and responsive, and registers my swipes and touches consistently. The raise-to-wake feature works 90% of the time, but could be slightly improved.

The watch is perfect for me in that it provides accurate activity tracking and some other simple information (like weather and time), without any distractions. I have it connected to my phone through the Zepp app (which is surprisingly decent and has improved even in the last month), but I don't have any of my notifications sent to my watch. The only times that my watch vibrates and notifies me are when it detects that I have been sitting for a while and it encourages me to stand up and do some exercises, which is helpful!

GPS, heart-rate tracking and step-counting have all been accurate in my experience, tracking my outdoor runs and indoor workouts seamlessly. My activity syncs automatically with Strava, which simple to set up. There are a good variety of watch faces (~50), and some of them are customizable with different activity metrics or information, which is also great. There are a decent number of apps / features in the app menu, ranging from a Pomodoro Timer to a breathing trainer to Amazon Alexa. Most have been simple to understand and use, but I haven't found myself using them often.

The one really killer feature that I have mostly taken for granted (because it's so non-invasive!) is the unbelievable battery life. The watch arrived at ~50% battery, and even with all the messing around with the watch and setup that I did in the first week, it still lasted a good week. Since then, I have charged it only twice, getting upwards of 10 days per charge. My wife has an Apple Watch Series 3, and she has to charge it much more frequently, which gets annoying.

Overall, great buy with a few minor flaws that don't impact the functionality of the watch. Buying this has made me more aware of my activity (or lack thereof), but hasn't provided any further distractions and is almost invisible in my daily life. Big win in my book.

title: The SpO2 sleep report is useless
text:
I replaced by Garmin and got my bluetooth Watch4 directly from Samsung, on sale, and with a military discount. That made it a better deal than Amazon's. One feature I was hoping would be better, after reading the experiences of people with Watch3 was the SpO2 sleep measurement since I have sleep apnea. I've been getting low reports of 70-75%. I should be brain dead and possibly dead, period. Good thing I have a Lookee Pro Ring Sleep Monitor that interfaces with my PC. It's very accurate and is dedicated for SpO2 and heart rate during sleep. The Watch4 just doesn't do SpO2 reliably, so if you have sleep apnea, look for some other way to track your O2 like a CMS-50 or a Lookee ring.

I've not had any problems with the battery life. I charge it every evening and I don't use the gps. I know where I live and how to get home (it's sewn into my shirt sleeves, jackets, cap).

I had trouble getting the watch to interact with my Galaxy phone, but one of Samsung's techs knew what to do about that (3 others didn't).

I installed Sleep Cycle in the watch since it checks for snoring. I'm a little insulted since I seldom snore because I wear a dental appliance made to stop snoring and ward off apnea by. Maybe it's picking up my wife's snore. Maybe I should have her sleep downstairs in the guest room to see if it still detects snoring.

The watch is great for automatically detecting some of my exercise. I don't bother telling the watch what I'm doing like walking across the living room to do some free weight exercise. It tends to notice exercising after a few minutes without my telling it. I think I set the auto-detect feature.

It has neat watch faces. I'm happy with what's available.

It's not super accurate with measuring heart rate. It's all over the place, even while I'm just typing this review. It went from high 50s to high 70s to mid-60s in just a few seconds. Back to 77. My fingertip oximeter tells a different story: 50 bpm and SpO2 97%. Yeah, the watchband is tight and about 2 cm above my wrist, Samsung. Skin and back of watch are clean. If the band were any tighter, my fingers would turn blue.

text: It would make for a decent smartwatch if not for issues, some of which make it unusable. Both my wife and I have a Samsung Galaxy S22 Ultra (US version). I also have a Galaxy Watch4 US version which paired with my US S22 Ultra. I purchased an additional Galaxy Watch4 for my wife from an official Samsung Store while on a trip in China. I can't even pair her watch and phone, regardless of the hours I wasted trying all sorts of "tricks" recommend by others with the same issue, online. Samsung's "customer service" is as bad as it gets, they never responded AT ALL to ANY of my emails. I'll make only one additional comment regarding battery life: 3 days claimed by Samsung is either a joke or intentionally misleading (read lie). Maybe (and even then it's only a maybe) if you fully charge it and then leave it on a desk untouched for 3 days with all functions turned off and minimum amount of apps installed (factory installed apps?). Even so, very misleading. Personally, I would not buy this watch again unless it cost $100 or less. Either way, friendly reminder, make sure you buy the same country version as your mobile phone, otherwise you won;t even be able to pair them ("thanks" Samsung!). Furthermore, as others have said, some of the watch's best functions/capabilities will only work with a Samsung phone and/or based on the phone's sim card (yes, Samsung will "read" your sim's card mobile provider and activate/deactivate functions based on that. In other words, even if you have a US mobile phone, if your sim card/mobile provider is foreign, the watch's functions/apps  - like "Health Monitor" - will work or not work based on your mobile provider country). Too many issues to make this watch a top contender. In fact, in my opinion, it's FAR from a top contender. Personally I'll never buy another Samsung watch and obviously wouldn't recommend it to others either.

text:
First, make you use the correct application to sync your watch to your phone. If you look for “Wear OS” on your phone in the Google play store it’s going to give you the Google application (WRONG). You want the Samsung “Wear” app from the Galaxy store. Use that and follow the prompts and it’ll set up your your phone and sync your watch just fine. I chose the Bluetooth option because I’m not giving Verizon one more nickel of my money. If you’re a Verizon customer you know exactly what I’m talking about.
Battery life: I would say I’m probably a light to moderate user. I put the watch on at 6 in morning, I’ll use it to answer phone calls, sometimes send a text message, check my notifications, start and stop my Podcasts. It does a really good job automatically tracking your workouts. It will do your sleep quite well if you wear it at night. I’ll put it back on the charger at 10 o’clock at night and it still has 50% battery. If I wear it all night I’ll drain the battery down to maybe 20%.
Calls: there was a slight learning curve for me, first smart watch. Answering calls, dismissing calls, etc. I didn’t quite have the hang of the touch and the swipe. Now that I do - extremely easy. I’ve only once used it to take a phone call without having my earbuds on. I had no trouble hearing the caller although they sound like they’re Lilliputian. The caller had no problem hearing me. It was kind of nice I was able to move around the room without carrying my phone with me.
Text: You have to do voice to text, or else use the short answer option. I prefer voice to text, so no problem here. The only not so good thing is I am a Verizon customer and they have their own Messages plus application which really works pretty well for my purposes since I run a business off my phone. I can’t use that application on the watch so I have reverted back to using Samsung‘s own text app. Not a big deal I’ll live.
Utilities: there’s the stopwatch, the alarm, the calculator, the calendar, you name it, there’s an app on the watch for that.
Oh, it tells time too. 😂

title: Good Watch and software but some significant shortcomings
text: I have had the watch 4 for 5 months and overall it is a good fitness tracker and sports watch but it has some significant short comings. It is a beautiful design even though I prefer the square or rectangular designs of the Fitbit. The display is clear and easy to see though the font could be a little larger to increase visibility especially when moving as in exercise. Navigating the menus on the watch face is easy and the screen is very responsive even with a glass screen protector in place. Swiping takes you easily across and a simple tap allows you to measure various things. Sleep tracking is good but I am not sure of the interpretation. I have been wearing this watch and a fitbit versa 3 to bed for 4 months and am yet to get both watches to agree as to the sleep stages. I get the impression-that the Fitbit better records REM sleep and the Galaxy Deep sleep but sometimes the parameters are reversed. Similarly in comparing the two watches for walking exercise, while the steps are similar the distances are different. I am further evaluating this parameter to see which is more accurate. The parameters for exercise recorded on the watch are very good. The wear OS installed on the phone gives very good reporting both of sleep and exercise data. The exercise data is particularly extensive and informative. The GPS works well. The O2 sat monitor 80% of the time it is triggered manually probably due to insensitivity , but it giges better readings for Oxygen levels during sleep. The graph showing sleep oxygen in the phone interpases is small and dingy and just give a crude idea of what time during the night your O2 levels fall below 90%. This can be improved. The body composition monitor is very good and though difficult to say if it is accurate it seems to follow the right trend over time. The major drawbacks. No matter what you turn off to save on battery power this watch has to be charged every day. A watch of this quality should have a better battery life.I charge at night before wearing to bed and have had it die in the middle of an exercise walk the following evening 18 hours later. I dont comment on the on screen rotating bezel as this is permanently turned off to save on the battery. Even with this we cant get 24 hrs. I was also extremely disappointed to find that the ECG did not work in my area. The choice of watch faces i find is also limited and not as interesting as some of the competitors . Overall a good watch but some major short comings . Three stars only

title: Loving my new fitness watch
text:
I am loving my new Garmin Venu SQ fitness watch. I'm just starting on a journey to get my body back in shape after a couple of really hard years. As a former professional athlete, I find that having lots of quantifiable information about my activity and how my body is functioning helps me with both my motivation and my ability to plan workouts.

The reason that I'm giving this 4 stars instead of 5 is because Garmin Fitness does not allow men to track menstrual cycles. This is a pain for a trans man who has the musculature and metabolism of a man because of testosterone shots but who still gets periods. It's important to track those cycles because it can hint at what's happening with the cycles of T uptake beyond what blood tests every 3 months might tell me. It's also important for cis men to be able to track their partner's cycle's if they are trying to conceive or if they are using fertility data to avoid conceiving, so not having this option at all is a major software fail. I'm not saying that menstrual tracking should be automatically on the watch, but if you turn it on, it should work without telling you "that's not available with your gender settings."

I have contacted Garmin Fitness about this and they have opened a software ticket which will hopefully lead to a change in the future. Other people contacting them to let them know that men should have the ability to track their own or their partner's cycles will help move this up their feature priority list.

title: I really like this watch!
text: I like Samsung products in general. They usually look great and function well.  I don't need a smartwatch, so I don't use it 24/7. But I think the Galaxy Watch 4 is a great piece of tech and it's so sleek and attractive. I'm a female w/small wrists but it doesn't look too bulky on me. I have a Galaxy S20 phone and it works nicely w/the watch. I love the ability to change watch bands, and the array of watch faces you can choose from, that you can also customize. Navigation on the watch works well and the display is large enough to see things. I like the digital bezel and have never accidently toggled it but I think the rotating bezel is cool too. The galaxy wearable app is straightforward and easy to use. Also syncs well w/Samsung health app for keeping track of health measurements. I used it to track my sleeping and the info was helpful. When smartphones can accurately track blood pressure I think that'll be my next purchase-I know some have this feature but the accuracy not there yet. It measures stress levels, ECG, and body composition. The watch allows you to receive/respond/answer phone calls, messages, emails. You have the option of transferring calls to/from phone. I was looking at pics someone texted me and they were very clear on the watch, so the display is pretty crisp. The cons for me-battery life-I get maybe 2 days max and I'm not a heavy user. If I use it all day then it definitely needs to be charged at night or first thing in the morning. It does charge up fairly quickly though. I can listen to music w/headphones through my phone and then control it using the watch. But I didn't see an easy way to download music to the watch itself. If you have a premium Spotify account you are able to download playlists but I don't have that type of account. Overall, I really like this watch-it's attractive, well-built, you get a lot of features/functionality for the price and works well w/Samsung Galaxy phones. I would definitely recommend it.

title: No Warranty from Amazfit / Zepp
text: One of the main reasons that I bought this watch was because of the "One Year Warranty". Unfortunately no warranty (other than Amazon's 60 days) exists.  After struggling with it for 3 months I contacted Amazfit support and they told me to get Amazon to take it back. It was beyond Amazon's A-Z warranty so I pointed that out to them. The sleep tracker was less than 50% accurate and the heart monitor kept giving erratic readings every couple of hours. I asked for my watch to be repaired or replaced (I did NOT want a refund). Over a series of emails every 48 hours for a month they had me jump through so many hoops that I thought I was running an obstacle course. Among the hoops (but not limited to) were sending pictures and screenshots, tightening the strap, then loosening the strap,  then shaving my wrist, then behaviour tagging etc etc. The list goes on and on. Every time I asked them to fix it they came up with another series of assignments or tests to try with the watch and would not take it back for repair.  This wasted a HUGE amount of my time. After 1 month, I  quit. They won. They would not take it back but instead would just continue to ask me to try or report different things til I would break and yes I finally broke. It was a master class in both conflict avoidance and passive-aggressive customer service.  Do not buy this watch if you want a warranty as none exists.

title: Galaxy Watch4 off to a slow start, but promising!
text:
I ordered my Watch4 directly from Samsung and have had it for a couple weeks now. I"ve noticed a few steps back from the Tizen OS on the Active and Active 2:

First and foremost, Starting a swim exercise puts the watch in water lock mode (as it should), but the buttons don't work in water lock mode, so the only way to pause or finish a swim is to take it out of water lock mode, then hope you or the watch aren't too wet to pause or finish by touching the screen. Not at all intuitive for this workout. The previous versions paused/resumed when you touched the physical button (worked in water lock mode, though you still had to take it out of water lock to "finish"). On a positive note, the watch tracks laps MUCH better than its predecessors!

Second, the only way you get notification that your rest time is over when working out in sets of reps is if you activate the screen by turning your wrist or touching it. It will probably tell you your rest is up if you activate the "always on" display, but the old versions didn't require that. This is a minor inconvenience, but something that worked fine on Tizen. This issue with all workout notifications seeming to "sleep" unless using the "always on" display causes several issues, actually, related to finishing workouts and apparently general gps tracking, as well. It left out 2 miles of a 5 mile cycling exercise because I hit "finish" before it had a chance to notify me how I did on "lap 3" and return to active tracking (I ended up manually entering the mileage as another workout using the phone app) and it regularly cuts off around 1/10 of a mile through inaccuracy (the previous models were far more accurate without having to be "always on").

Third, you used to have an option for multiple multi-workout shortcut tiles. Now you get one, and it will have the exact same workouts that are in the Health app under exercise (changing the shortcuts in the app changes them on the watch and vice versa). This is also just a minor inconvenience, and I'm already used to choosing workouts from the list, which is conveniently organized by most recently used.

One last thing I find strange is that every time I reach my steps goal, the watch congratulates me on meeting my goal for the first time. On my Active, I got a simple message that I met my goal, but with the Watch 4, I meet my goal for the first time all the time. Changing the goal doesn't stop this.

I intend to stick with it because I have to believe this is related to the new OS and updates will address some or all of these issues. It's very new, after all, and likely that none of these points will be relevant in another 3 or 4 months.

title: Truly a smart watch with nice added health stuff
text:
Look, by and large it's a great watch. The health tracking features are nice, although the step count (which is presumably based on stride) varies VASTLY from what Fitbit tracks (i'm talking at least one thousand steps per 5k, which probably makes sense since Fitbit's stride algorithm is propritary) and, as everyone says, the battery life is pretty horrible.

This watch goes above and beyond the Versa 2 in that you can set up fall alerts to go out to people, as well as "personal safety" alerts and you can see the images in texts, emails, etc. on your watch. They're not the easiest all the time, as the watchface is the size limit, but still, that's awesome, at least to someone coming from a Versa and being over the text notification just being "image." As someone not old enough to want to have a life alert thing, but living alone, that's nice. There are some other nice features as well, but I can't think of them right now.

On to the battery life: you can make your watch battery last 24 hours (maybe a smidge more) by having it on power saver for most of those 24 hours. Everything still works as a smart watch/fitness tracker should, you just have to push a side button or double tap the screen to turn on your display. It feels kind of lame to do that, but again, 24 or more hours without having to put it on the charger is nice, especially when without that, you're probably looking at 8 hours per charge, without changing any of the features that make your Samsung Galaxy 4 a smart watch and tracker.

As I implied, coming from a Versa 2, that was a little bit of a bitter pill. However, as this watch has no trouble maintaining its bluetooth connection to my Samsung phone, unlike the Versa 2, and has heaps more features, I personally felt the like the tradeoff wasn't the worst ever. YMMV.

title: Battery Life was questionable
text:
I bought a Galaxy Watch Active 2 during pre-orders a few years ago, I really enjoyed the watch until (I'm assuming) a water mishap rendered the touch screen iffy at best. I don't need the latest and greatest so I figured I'd be able to buy a "like new" Galaxy Watch 4 for way cheaper instead of waiting for the Galaxy Watch 5 to be released for (I was assuming) a higher price.

My main concern with the watch was the battery life, it seemed to under-perform compared to my Galaxy Watch Active 2 when using the same settings and watch face I used on my previous watch. Besides the ECG (which was supposed to be included in the 2) it didn't seem like there were all that many improvements. That's not a huge issue to me because I really just need a watch that does some smartwatch basics.

The design on the 2 is a bit different than the 4, not necessarily in a bad way, but the band... I absolutely hated! The way they added the bit to contour right against the watch face made it look quite bad and fit weird on my small wrist. The contour is squared off on top and bottom of the band, so if you have a small wrist like me (I'd really consider my wrist average for a female) the watch face takes up most of the top of your wrist and the watch band needs to go almost straight 'down' to wrap around my wrist, however, due to how the bands contour is squared off, the squared off edge ends up catching on the body of the watch and either you have to squish it which makes it go at a legitimate 90 degree angle exposing the side of the contour making it look weird and pinched on the wrist, OR it gets stuck on the face and looks like the band is bulging off the side of the watch face, all of which looks awkward on my wrist.
I feel like this could have been easily resolved with rounding off the bottom of the contour on the band. If i were to have kept it i probably would have trimmed up the bottom squared off edge to a more rounded finish to let it more more freely on my wrist. The contour itself looks nice on a larger wrist like my husbands but its just not visually appealing of very functional for a small wrist.

The combination of all these factors led me to return the watch, I feared that the "used" factor could have played some part in the battery's questionable performance. I made the decision to return the watch, wait for the announcement of the Galaxy Watch 5 and weigh the pros and cons of re-buying the 4 in "NEW" condition OR spending more and getting the brand new Galaxy Watch 5. Once they announced the Galaxy Watch 5 (about 10 days ago) I compared the pricing, specs, etc. .... Ordering through Samsung, during pre-orders, I was able to use a promo code to get $50 worth of accessories on top of the wireless charger duo (which is also available with amazons pre-order of the watch) but what pushed me to go through Samsung for the pre-order was their trade in deal (trade in ANY functioning smart watch for a minimum of $75 up to $165(I'm trading in an old fitbit for $75)) In the end I was able to get the 'latest and greatest' for almost the exact same price as the Used- "Like New" watch I returned.

title: Great if you have a Samsung phone
text:
Pros:
+ Light
+ Battery better than expected (details later)
+ Convenient
+ Good use of screen
+ ECG and body composition measurements with Samsung phone
+ Half brightness is still pretty bright

Cons:
- Fitness tracking can be iffy
- Some features require a Samsung phone
- Not sure about ECG but the body composition feature isn't really accurate. It's a watch so it's not meant to be super accurate.

Battery life:
I have always on display turned off, brightness set to about quarter to half brightness, heart rate monitor measuring continuously, NOT on airplane mode. I also have it set up such that when raise my wrist to look at my watch, the screen turns on. The battery lasts far longer than a day for me. I'm not sure what those other reviewers are doing to kill the battery so quickly. My guess is they have the brightness at 100% and always on display turned on as well as a bunch of other features/apps running in the background. Of course that would kill the battery...

Fitness tracking:
The watch always detects workouts late as well as when they stop. I would say it takes a minute before it "realizes" I have stopped doing some activity. Another thing is that the app kind of sucks when it comes to this. I lift more than anything and a good majority of the stuff I do isn't listed. Furthermore, I just want to know how long I have been active, my heart rate, and an estimate of the calories I have burned. The app makes it a bit annoying to do this. I definitely liked the simplicity of the FitBit app more. Also, the heart rate monitor can be finicky when I'm sweating heavily. Sometimes it just can't detect my heart rate. I guess that's just a limitation of smart watches in general though (if you want an accurate and precise hr monitor, get a chest strap).

Body composition:
It's decent for what it is. Measurements are never accurate (it says my body fat percentage is 30+ but I know I'm closer to the 20-25 range). It measures BMI, water weight, muscle weight, and a few other details too. Like I said before, it's a watch so measurements won't be very accurate, but you can at least measure relative change over time.

Like many others have said, ECG and body composition measurements require a Samsung phone. I can see this is a deal breaker for many as it's the same crap Apple pulls. Luckily I do have a Samsung phone.

Overall I would say it is great for what it is: an all-around smart watch for the everyday person with the $$$ for one. If you are looking for a watch specifically for fitness. I would suggest the Apple watch, Garmins, Polars, and of course FitBit for the budget-concious.

title: A huge disappointment for a Garmin device
text: I have owned a Garmin Vivoactive HR for years with no issues and confidently bought the Venu SQ for my wife to track skiing and biking.  The Venu SQ has been a major disappointment from the start.  It's a beautiful looking device and my wife was initially very excited to have it.  Regrettably, those are the only two positives.  Once configured, the Venu SQ took forever (5+ minutes) to sync data to an iPhone after a single activity had been completed.  After completing an activity, the Venu SQ frequently displayed messages that it was low on memory and the activity data may be lost.  Recently, the Garmin Connect software showed a firmware update was available but it could not be applied because the Venu SQ didn't have enough memory available - even though all activity had been sync'd to Garmin Connect.  I bought this for the Ski app based on my experience with the Vivoactive HR Ski app.  We quickly learned the Ski app on the Venu SQ does not auto-lap between runs, presumably because it does not have an altimeter sensor.  You have to manually push a button at the end of each ski run to tell the SQ you have started a new run.  More than once my wife started a specific workout activity but the SQ tracked it as something else.  After months and months of frustration, we've given up on the Venu SQ and have replaced it with an Apple Watch Series 6.  Maybe the Venu SQ functions well as a very basic fitness device, but a lot of our time with jt was spent dealing with software and other technical shortcomings.

title: Good outweighs Bad
text:
The GOOD: this watch has virtually every feature you could possibly ask for in a modern smartwatch. There are actual working WearOS apps for all the important functions out there, and they all work very well for the most part. The watch-face customization options are incredible, and the two buttons are perfect in execution every time (I have my top button set to launch Google Pay with a double-tap, which has been fantastic for quick checkouts over the past month).

I love the wealth of options available - vibration length and intensity are adjustable, and there are even multiple vibration patterns to choose from (for example, one of them is called dubstep and is just as annoying as it sounds lol). I love the simple option which silences phone notifications while you're wearing the watch (no need for duplicate notifications), which is smart enough to turn itself off the instant you remove the watch from your wrist. It just works. There are many other multitudes of detail I could go into, but you've probably already read about them. Let's just say overall, the watch is great!

The BAD: battery life. Definitely less than 24 hours with moderate use and always-on display. I don't understand how people use it all day and then keep it on at night for sleep tracking. This thing needs its overnight charge. With a high amount of notifications coming in, I've noticed dramatically worse battery life. As in, full charge at 8am to start work day and then it's at 20% when I get home at 5 or 6. If you wanted to take this thing on a multi-day camping trip (I know, odd use case), it would last exactly one day before becoming useless unless you packed a charger for it. I suppose I'm really hammering this point home, but I came from a Pebble 2 (finally broke, sniff sniff) which lasted at least 7 days regardless of heavy use... so this watch's battery life was a bit of a shock for me.

Also a bit underwhelming to me was the fact that this watch, although being touted as the flagship watch for Wear OS 3, is VERY MUCH a Samsung watch. I was expecting to be able to use Google's Wear OS app to set it up. Nope, you need the Samsung Wear app plus another Samsung app specifically configured for the galaxy watch 4, PLUS the Wear OS app if you want certain functionality to work (like the camera app). That's 3 phone apps to run this watch in all its glory. Not to mention, it comes preloaded with about a dozen Samsung apps on it, which you can't remove without rooting the watch (which I have no interest in doing). Ultimately, I was expecting more of a pure Google experience, but ended up with a lot more Samsung than I bargained for.

All that being said, the watch is still a marvel of technology. In my opinion, the good outweighs the bad in this case. I love the watch, and will continue to use it heavily until Google finally releases the fabled Pixel watch.

title: It's almost the best.
text:
TL;DR - If you're looking for a high-end smartwatch look elsewhere. If you're looking for an above average fitness watch you read the rest.

Bought this to kick my butt into getting healthier post 2020 and have a smartwatch at the same time. So far so good! I went with Garmin since they are more focused on physical activity and being active. This fits the bill almost nicely. The cons are the standouts here. The sleep tracking is...sketch. Once you set your bedtime via the app if you lie down in bed and don't move...it'll think your asleep. lie still long enough and you'll be in REM sleep...all while lying awake and staring at the ceiling. It's useful for tracking my pulse ox while I sleep and to get a rough idea of when I get in bed and out. Other con is music. I got the Music Venu Sq for the ability to load stuff onto it so I could leave my cellphone at home if I go running or on a neighborhood walk. It works but you need to load it though your computer. And as a YouTube music subscriber (long story), there is no watch app to use the service as of 02/14/2021. If I carry my phone I can stream it through my watch to my headphones... a little more convoluted than I'd like.

The health stats (outside sleep) are pretty amazing and the app goes into even further detail. In addition to your normal run tracker and other basics in that vein It connects to MyFitnessPal for calorie tracking, Garmin Golf for golfing activities, you can even swim in this thing! I personally love that it includes yard work, yoga and meditation as activities that contribute to your overall "intensity minutes" score.

Battery lasts for days on days. I charge it once every 6 days or so once the battery gets to 10%. It pairs quickly and has a decent range.

As a smartwatch it's ok. You can set up a few quick replies for texts...but that's about the height of it's smarts. Can't use it Dick Tracy style to talk to people.

title: I highly recommend this watch, especially if you have a Samsung phone
text:
I bought the 40 mm version and with its round face fits perfectly on my smaller male wrist. Use 1 less notch than really tight to slip the strap inside - not having a strap end pointing out of my wrist was 1 big reason I like the Watch4. It's loose enough to still read heart rate, etc. and light enough I don't feel its on me.

Other cheaper smartwatches were inaccurate, some apps didn't work, and nothing intuitive and no help how to do something or solve a problem. it was worth my sanity and satisfaction to go up in price.

I picked the watch face I liked the best and used the 5 areas to customize what would appear - I chose date/time with Vietnam time, temperature, battery life, swimming pool mode and messages. I easily set up and ordered other watch apps and just swipe left to see each "tile." using google search on my laptop I found how to install other apps on my Watch4... I installed Google Pay because it's better/easier than Samsung pay. Swimming is the only exercise routine I do so I didn't want to have to search through many exercises just to get to swimming, and I could chose swimming pool to get laps (it erroneously call them lengths... a length if from 1 end to the other, half a lap)... or god forbid swimming in the ocean. at the end I push a button for 2 seconds which expels any water and you can actually hear it do so. some of the setup up is done on the phone app (Wear) and some directly on the watch. Samsung make the watch very close in functions/swiping to its phone.
beware it doesn't appear you can use the phone wireless charger, must use the mini-wirless charger included. the battery easily last a day plus hours and when I'm totally used to it the watch won't be using as much energy and so last longer. at this point, it's fine to connect to its charger for 1-2 hours to fully charge back up.
In summary, I rarely am so positive about a product and paid the full Amazon price.
